- U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced the creation of an Office of Religious Affairs at the Department of Defense on Sept. 30, 2026, during a speech he called the "State of the Force" address.
- Hegseth suggested the Office of Religious Affairs would address urgent spiritual needs among the troops, which he said had long been neglected. He said the office would report directly to him and that budgets would be guaranteed both for chaplaincy and infrastructure, such as "base chapels."
- Hegseth said that "less than 5% of our force identifies as non-religious," without citing his source for the number. A 2019 congressional report found that while 2.3% of the force identified as agnostic or atheist, the affiliation of 24.4% of active duty personnel fell under "Other/Unclassified/Unknown."
- Snopes will update this report if, or when, additional information surfaces. We have reached out to the DOD to ask what concrete actions the office will take. We also reached out to the American Humanist Association and are waiting for responses.
In October 2026, a rumor spread that U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth had announced the creation of an Office of Religious Affairs at the Pentagon.
The claim spread on social media, including X. One X post included a video of Hegseth speaking on a stage with a U.S. flag background (archived):
"Today, at my direction, I am establishing the Office of Religious Affairs," Hegseth says in the video. "Starting today, and for secretaries of war after me, the Office of Religious Affairs will report straight to the top. No staff filters. No bureaucratic dilution. A direct line to the secretary."
Meanwhile, several Snopes readers searched the website seeking more information about the supposed Office of Religious Affairs.
It is true that on Sept. 30, 2026, Hegseth gave a speech he called the "State of the Force" address. In this speech, he said he had ordered the creation of an office dedicated to religious affairs, which Department of Defense spokesperson Sean Parnell confirmed in an X post (archived):
We reached out to the DOD seeking more details about the initiative and will update this story if we learn more.
Here's what we know about the new DOD office so far:
Office of Religious Affairs
In his speech, Hegseth said the initiative would address what he described as long-neglected spiritual needs among the troops (starting around the 50:25 mark of the DOD's recording of the speech):
After describing how significant the loss of a religious community could be for military personnel assigned to a new location or deployed abroad, Hegseth said that "political correctness and secular humanism" had allowed budgets for religious support to dwindle and infrastructure such as "base chapels" to go into disarray.
Religious diversity in the force
Hegseth said that "less than 5% of our force identifies as non-religious," without citing his source for the number. A 2019 congressional report found that while 2.3% of the force identified as agnostic or atheist, the affiliation of 24.4% of active duty personnel fell under "Other/Unclassified/Unknown" (PDF Page 51).
Meanwhile, the Military Association of Atheists and Freethinkers, an organization that advocates for nonreligious military members but is not associated with the DOD, said 2.05% of the force identified as "Humanists" in 2018 (Humanism is a non-theistic belief; Humanists believe in a moral and ethical code without believing in God). That report also said the chaplaincy did not represent the religious diversity of the military, with an overrepresentation of evangelistic Christians, when only 13.31% of the troops identified as such.
We reached out to the MAAF for comment on the creation of the office. A spokesperson told us the group was in the process of dissolving and directed us to the American Humanist Association, a nonprofit that advocates for secular humanism. We will update this story if the AHA returns our request for a statement on the possible impact of the creation of the office on nonreligious service members.
In May 2026, the DOD released a list of recognized religions in a memorandum signed by Undersecretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata. The memo included 31 religions, down from 211, according to Military.com, the news outlet dedicated to reporting on the U.S. Military. Twenty-two of those 31 were Christian denominations.
Hegseth then announced the creation of the Office of Religious Affairs, designed to report directly to him in the Pentagon organizational chart. In his announcement, he said (around 52:32 of the video embedded above):
This won't be a paper pushing shop. It will have real teeth. It will protect budgets, demand infrastructure, and strengthen religious support. The experts, our chaplains, will finally have an advocate at the highest levels. Policy and resources will serve the mission, not smother the mission.
'Spiritual readiness' and 'spiritual resilience'
A memo issued on the same day confirmed the creation of the office. It read, in part:
The Department of War is committed to fulfilling its duty to support the Department's Service members, their families, and the Department's civilian personnel in the free exercise of religion as protected by the Constitution of the United States and applicable Federal law. While the Department accomplishes this mission primarily through the chaplaincies of the Military Departments established under title 10, U.S. Code, the establishment of the ORA will ensure resources are adequately provided and, where necessary, policy is properly aligned to prioritize the free exercise of religion and the spiritual readiness across the Total Force.
Still, Hegseth's memo said, this effort to support the spirituality of military personnel should not "be construed to compel religious participation or to diminish the free exercise rights of any Service member, civilian employee, or family member of any faith or no faith."
The memo also said the new office had 90 days to present a plan of action to rebuild the spiritual force of the military:
Within 90 days of the date of this memorandum, the Secretaries of the Military Departments, in coordination with their respective Chiefs of Chaplains, will submit to the Director a comprehensive baseline report of all unfunded and underfunded religious affairs requirements, including, but not limited to, delivery ofreligious ministry, facilities and infrastructure, logistics, chaplain-led programs, chapel youth programs, faith-based homeschool support for military families, programs related to suicide reduction, and contracted services from faith-based non-Federal entities; research, technology, and analytical tools to support spiritual fitness, spiritual readiness, and spiritual resilience; chaplain in-service procurement programs, chaplain and religious support team training and education.
For further reading, Snopes examined another announcement Hegseth made that day, the launch of "Project Meridian," set to study the "future of warfare."

Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two
- Published
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first such military execution in more than 60 years.
Nidal Malik Hasan, a US Army major and physician, fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.
It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.
Hasan was convicted of 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted murder by a jury panel of 13 officers, which unanimously recommended his death sentence.
Parnell said the Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution.
"Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," he wrote on X.
Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".
He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.
The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.
The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.
Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.
A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.
It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.
The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.
Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.
The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.
Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.
Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.
Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025.
Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty.
The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

Polish film and TV luminary Darius Jabloński’s spy thriller “Fortel” and Estonia’s “Stormbird” from multi-awarded Kadri Kousaar (“Magnus,” “Mother”) feature in the lineup of Tallinn’s TV Beats Co-Financing Market, running over Nov. 16-17.
They are joined by Spain’s “When Devils Rule” from Rodrigo Susarte (“Patagonia”), and Belgium’s “The Inheritance” powered by “This is Not a Murder Mystery” producer Panenka.
Picked among 50 submissions from Eurimages member states, the 10 selected series will vie for the coveted €50,000 ($56,000) Council of Europe Series Co-Production Development Award.
Popular on Variety
“Never before have we welcomed that many big names and companies,” said Petri Kemppinen, co-head of TV Beats, alongside Roosa Toivonen.
This year’s crop hails from Belgium, Czechia, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, and co-production partner Canada. As underscored by Toivonen, the geographical spread mirrors TV Beats’ core which is “to act as a bridge between the Baltics, Central Eastern Europe, and the Nordics. Three territories – Czechia, Finland, and Estonia – topped the list of applications.

Full rundown of TV Beats Co-Financing Market lineup:
	“Breaking the Ice” (“Päike mis sulatab jääd,” 6X45’, Estonia)
Young adult drama from Estonian powerhouse Zolba Productions (“Von Fock”, “My Dear Mother,” “A Girl From Tallinn”), co-penned and co-created by the seasoned Leana Jalukse (“Mother”, “Von Fock”) and German screenwriting expert Joachim Friedmann.
Beneath the polished surface of Estonia’s elite ice rinks, a Russian hockey prodigy ruled by his violent father and an Estonian figure skater groomed by a manipulative coach fall in love across a national divide. “Breaking the Ice” is not another fast-paced feel-good love story on skates,” says producer Jevgeni Supin. “Our series looks beneath the polished surface of youth sport, where abuse by parents and coaches is often disguised as pursuit for excellence. At its heart, it’s is a story about two young people who find the courage, through love, to break this cycle.”
“Fortel” (8X45’, Poland)
Legendary Polish film mogul and director Dariusz Jabłoński (“The Pleasure Principle,” “The Cop-A New Chapter”), serves as creator and showrunner of this spy thriller penned by US screenwriter Marc Grey, episodic writer of Apple TV’s International Emmy-winning show “Tehran.”
	Jabłoński’s own pedigreed banner Apple Film Production is producing for commercial giant Polsat.
The core of the action is the little-known Polish town of Rzeszów close to the Ukraine border which has turned into a spy nest and arms dealing platform. The story tracks a CIA officer who sets a trap for Russian saboteurs, targeting confidential Western arms shipments while secretly searching for his missing brother, who may hold the key to the leak, says the logline.
	
“Fortel” is about the history we’re living through right now, in real time, two hours from my home,” Jabłoński tells Variety. “Rzeszów is a city that woke up one morning to find itself at the center of the war, with no instruction manual and no way out. I want to make a thriller that feels the way the war feels – chaotic, morally unresolved and shot through with unexpected moments of humanity, with a cast drawn from several of the countries involved. A Polish-based story that the whole world needs to see right now,” he claims.
“Happy New Year!” (“Laimingų Naujų!” 10X21’, Lithuania)
Created and helmed by rising talent Montis Norvaisis for his outfit Big Drama, setup with producer Lineta Lasiauskaitė. The drama turns on a young woman, victim of spike drinking at a lavish New Year’s Eve party in a remote manor. When the guests refuse to confront the crime, her best friend seeks justice herself. Norvaisis will draw from his own experience to portray a raw and authentic portrait of New Year’s Eve youth parties.
	“Kalmann” (6X45’, Iceland, Finland, Estonia)
TV adaptation of Icelandic-Swiss crime author Joachim B. Schmidt’s “Kalmann” book series, penned by María Heba Þorkelsdóttir and Kristófer Dignus who directs.
Produced by Kontent’s Guðný Guðjónsdóttir and Sara Djeddou Baldursdóttir, who have attached Iceland’s main streamer Síminn and co-pro partners Snapper Films from Finland and Cuba Films from Estonia. Headlining the show is the eccentric sheriff Kalmann, who uses unique instincts to solve murders.
	“’Kalmann’ sits within the internationally established Nordic crime space, but brings warmth, humor, melancholy and humanity to the genre alongside a compelling murder investigation,” says Baldursdóttir, who plans to use TV Beats to test the show’s concept, tone and international potential. Production is set to start in the fall 2027.
“Intimacy on Prescription” (“Intimita na předpis, 8X60’, Czechia)
“Can good sex save every marriage,” says the logline about the tragicomedy set in 1970s Czechoslovakia, and inspired by the real story of Stanislav Kratochvíl, a pioneer of couples sex therapy. The show, helmed by established theater and film director Jiří Havelka (“Owners”), is set in a psychiatric clinic, where couples are invited to say out loud what society, marriage and shame have taught them to hide.
	“For us, ‘Intimacy’ is not only about sex, but about the courage to speak honestly about desire, fear, shame, power and the need to be seen by the person closest to you,” says producer Karolina Zalabáková, who looks forward to pitching in Tallinn this story “strongly rooted in Czech and Czechoslovak history” with “emotional themes that are universal and highly exportable.” The screenplay from head-writer Kristina Májová, co-written with Matěj Randár and Jan Smutný, is based on an original idea by Kateřina Kořínková.
“Stormbird” (“Tormilind,” 5X42’, Estonia)
	
Historical thriller from acclaimed filmmaker Kadri Kõusaar, credited for the Cannes Un Certain Regard’s “Magnus” and Estonia’s Oscar pick “Mother.” Set in 1949, under Soviet occupied Estonia. After killing soldiers who attack her family, Lee (18), known as ‘Stormbird’, becomes a fugitive and joins the Forest Brothers band led by “Geronimo” to rescue her imprisoned brother, Uku. Hunted by the Red Army, she fights to survive, while her childhood friend Reinhardt becomes her enemy. producer Aet Laigu says “Stormbird” “is first and foremost a story about people trying to survive and forced to make impossible choices under occupation.” It’s also a unique take of a “rarely seen part of European history”, depicted through a young woman’s eyes, turning on topical themes such as freedom, resistance and identity.
	“Tanner” (6X50’, Ireland, Canada)
Produced by Fíbín Films’ Bernie Hoban and Darach Ó Tuairisg, co-produced by Fraser Ash and Kevin Krikst for Canadian power-player Rhombus Media, attached to HBO’s Emmy nominated “The Sympathizer.”
The story created and penned by Keith Hodder, with Damian McCann and Sarah Gordon turns on a former Irish intelligence officer who returns home to investigate a missing teenager and uncovers a tech-powered conspiracy reaching from elite schools to the highest levels of government. Hoban says “Tanner” stands out thanks to its unique world “rarely seen before, the Irish intelligence services operating in a country whose prosperity is increasingly intertwined with some of the world’s most powerful multinational corporations, creating fascinating tensions between democracy, sovereignty and corporate influence.”” Through a uniquely Irish lens, “Tanner” tackles themes that resonate across the world while anchoring them in the journey of an unforgettable protagonist – a deeply flawed investigator whose greatest gift may also be his undoing,” she adds.
	“The Inheritance” (“De Erfenis,” 6X45’, Belgium)
From fast-expanding powerhouse Panenka behind the New8 hit show “This is Not a Murder Mystery” and Series Mania 2025 Special Mention winner “Putain.” Commissioned by leading Flemish broadcaster VTM.
Created and penned by Alexandra Jans with Jan Van Dyck for producers Kato Maes, Kristoffel Mertens and Karlijn Van de Cruys. Psychological thriller set against the world of animal welfare and hunting. When Hanne, a staff member of a struggling animal rescue, unexpectedly becomes executor of a wealthy hunting family’s estate, a bitter battle over the inheritance erupts. Van de Cruys says the show will draw from its breathtaking location-Belgium’s largest national park of Limburg’s Hoge Kempen, and the personal take from Jans who has crafted the story out of her own personal experience.
“The Woman Who Roared” (4X45’, Finland)
From box-office hit habitué, actor and filmmaker Pamela Tola (“Ladies of Steel,” “Bad Apples”). Dramedy in which the recently widowed Leena (65) discovers that the Helsinki Zoo is actually an arena where international spies gather. She believes the place is linked to a top-secret nuclear weapon her late husband had hidden.
“The Woman Who Roared” offers a fresh take on the spy genre – thrilling, funny, and full of heart,” says producer Mete Sasioglu of Sons of Lumière, who will be looking for co-producers, especially from France, Eastern Europe and the Nordics in Tallinn.
	“When Devils Rule” (“Los demones mandan,” 6X35’, Spain)
Darkly humorous political thriller with supernatural elements from the team behind Movistar Plus’ anticipated “Patagonia.” Atlantika Films’ Nano Arrieta-creator and producer with Claudia Ruíz — shares the writing room with Popy Blasco, Ibai Ariztegi and Bárbara Zemelman. In a world fractured by power, fear and political extremism, a group of women uncovers a demonic force operating at the highest level of society-and realizes the chaos around them may be part of a much darker design.

The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.
Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity.
On the flip side, El Niño is contributing to an extremely active period for tropical cyclones in the Pacific Ocean. After recent hurricanes in the eastern half of the basin, Super Typhoon Choi-Wan is now active and a category 4 typhoon to the south-east of Japan, while on a strengthening trend. After developing on 30 September, Choi-Wan moved through the Northern Mariana Islands as a tropical storm, causing power outages on the island of Tinian, forcing the closure of schools and government offices. Choi-Wan underwent rapid intensification after clearing the islands on Sunday, and as of Sunday night has sustained winds of 150mph, and gusts of up to 180mph. The system is expected to curve away from mainland Japan and areas affected by Typhoon Dujuan last month, while steadily weakening over the coming week.

Roughly 200 people are under medical observation, several hospitals are under quarantine, and dozens are in isolation in Russia following the unexplained death of an infectious disease researcher at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia, in the town of Shelekhov, according to early reports of the situation on Sunday and Monday.
Researcher Darya Shipilova reportedly died last week from pneumonia of “unknown” cause, according to Rospotrebnadzor, a Russian public health agency.
Unconfirmed information regarding her death has swirled. Some reports have claimed she accidentally broke a test tube containing the plague pathogen, Yersinia pestis, on September 25. She subsequently fell ill, was admitted to a hospital September 29 with severe pneumonia and died overnight between October 1 and Oct. 2. The head of the Russian region that neighbors Irkutsk, Alexey Tsydenov, initially reported that she had died of plague but later altered his statement to say she “possibly” died of the disease.
Y. pestis can cause several forms of plague: bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic—the latter of which can be aggressive and quickly fatal. However, the pathogen is generally easily treated by antibiotics. In the US, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends that anyone exposed to the pathogen should undergo an immediate 7-day post-exposure antibiotic prophylaxis treatment. Additionally, though pneumonic plague is spread via respiratory particles from coughing, it is not considered highly infectious; it requires direct, close contact for the bacteria to be transmitted.

Are there any disadvantages to using IMAX theaters?
Ticket availability and how much they cost can be important factors.
For a cinematic experience that is truly larger than life, you won't find many theater formats that rival IMAX. IMAX movies are among the biggest and loudest you'll ever watch. The entire experience is meant to be premium, a step above what you'll find in a typical screening. Few movies are truly made for IMAX, with Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey one of the most recent blockbuster standouts.
There are disadvantages to IMAX theaters, though. You can expect an IMAX ticket to cost more – if you can get one. The biggest showings are hard to book, if you're close to one anyway, with titles like The Odyssey only playing in IMAX 70mm at just 41 locations worldwide when it came to screens in July 2026. The format isn't automatically the best choice for a movie, either.
A bigger picture isn't always a better one
People go to IMAX movie theaters to enjoy big-screen pictures. IMAX releases feature an expanded aspect ratio compared to standard cinematic movies. Instead of the 2.39:1 widescreen ratio commonly used for blockbusters, IMAX movies can use 1.90:1 or 1.43:1 aspect ratios. The black space above and below a movie that you'll typically see is completely removed with an IMAX screening, with more of the movie filling your field of view.
Productions require specialist equipment to film it. IMAX films use either traditional 65mm IMAX film cameras, which are typically very loud, bulky and incredibly expensive. Movies which are "Filmed for IMAX" — like Tom Cruise's Mission Impossible: The Final Reckoning — use digital IMAX cameras to capture expanded footage, although they aren't shooting on the same large-format film stock. Either way, the effect is much the same: large landscapes end up feeling much bigger, and the action taking place across the entire screen seems much more immersive.
That wouldn't necessarily be a disadvantage for the watcher. You're probably not rushing to complain that a movie is too immersive. The problem is that a bigger frame can show you more without actually showing you anything better.
This is especially true for movies that haven't been made specifically for IMAX. Recent releases like Toy Story 5 and Moana have both screened in IMAX theaters without being classed by IMAX as "Filmed for IMAX." You're getting an IMAX screening, but if the movie wasn't shot with IMAX cameras or created with its aspect ratio, it won't be the same. Sure, it'll be bigger and louder, but you won't necessarily get the expanded aspect ratio and extra picture area that you'd expect from a movie made with IMAX in mind.
That can take away one of the strongest reasons to pay the premium. If I'm spending more on an IMAX ticket, I'll want to watch a film that actually makes use of the format in its truest format, rather than one that's simply been remastered to fit the screen.
You'll pay more for IMAX
Speaking of costs, buying an IMAX ticket will set you back more. IMAX is a premium format, and the cinemas that offer IMAX screenings are pricing it accordingly. Big chains including AMC and Regal explicitly apply surcharges for IMAX and other premium large-format screenings on top of their usual prices. How much you'll pay will vary, depending on the theater, location and screening but if you choose an IMAX viewing, you will almost certainly pay more.
That's easier to swallow if it's a movie specifically designed to take advantage of the grandeur of IMAX. Take The Odyssey, this year's darling of the IMAX world and the first Hollywood movie to be shot entirely on IMAX film. This is a movie that deserves to be seen on the biggest screen. The immersive scale of its production means that watching it in IMAX is part of the experience, rather than just an upgrade. You're not simply paying more to watch the same movie on a bigger screen.
I'm not entirely convinced that watching a showing of Minions and Monsters is quite the same. That's not a criticism of that particular movie: it applies just as much to Moana, Scream 7 or Masters of the Universe, all recent releases that also had IMAX screenings. These are just films that haven't been made with IMAX in mind. Their scale just isn't able to match, and you won't get the same experience from it.
So, if you're expecting to pay more, you want the best. The Odyssey and films to follow it sit at the top, filmed with 70mm IMAX film. IMAX Digital movies like the latest Mission Impossible movie go next. Everything else, it's probably worth just paying less and watching it on a standard cinema screen and not in an IMAX theater.
You won't find many true IMAX screens around
If you're certain you want to go watch a movie at an IMAX theater, there's likely one nearby. According to IMAX, there's 1,876 screens available across 91 different countries, although that number includes screens you'll find in museums and science centers, for instance.
Sounds good? Well, if you wanted to watch The Odyssey at IMAX in its true 70mm IMAX film, you'd have far less choice. Only 41 locations worldwide provided screenings for watching it on traditional IMAX 70mm film. There are far more IMAX-labeled screens, but these typically rely on digital projection rather than the physical 70mm film, so you're not necessarily enjoying the same experience.
So, what are you getting? Your local IMAX might still give you a huge screen and upgraded sound, but it could be a digital setup rather than the enormous 1.43:1, 70mm presentation that the critics are raving about. I travelled to watch The Odyssey for that very reason. I'm not sure I would do so for movies that are simply remastered for an IMAX screen, however.
The best movies mean a fight for tickets
So, you're ready to go to an IMAX theater, but there's a potential problem. You're up against 10,000 other people trying to find a ticket for a less-than-adequate number of screenings. Finding a seat could be tough when booking the biggest blockbusters.
The Odyssey once again proves the point. Tickets for its first IMAX 70mm screenings were put on sale a full year before it was released. 95 percent of the first batch were sold within a day, with many selling within minutes. Once it was released, IMAX claimed that the 41 theaters showing it in 70mm film were recording sellouts well into its run.
A sellout run is great for the movie business. Less so for the cinema-goer who wants to watch it. Likewise, if the best seats are sold out, you're not getting the best experience. Where you sit in an IMAX theater can make a real difference: you don't want to be craning your neck from the second row or sitting right at the edge of an enormous screen. If the best seats are gone, I'd rather choose another showing than pay extra for a worse view.
Booking early can fix that, but who's choosing to book a trip to the cinema far in advance? Yes, IMAX theaters can be worth it for the biggest pictures, but there are too many disadvantages to overcome at the moment for smaller films. With pricing and availability, along with packed screenings to deal with, IMAX theaters have a barrier to entry that, in most cases, makes them more hassle than a standard screening. Whether that's worth it will really be up to you.

Vaxcyte said Monday that its experimental pneumococcal vaccine hit the primary endpoints in a Phase 3 clinical trial, setting up the California-based biotech to compete with Pfizer and Merck.
Vaxcyte’s shot, VAX-31, is designed to protect against 31 serotypes, or strains, of bacteria that can cause pneumococcal disease, including pneumonia, compared to 20 strains for Pfizer’s Prevnar and 21 strains for Merck’s Capvaxive.
In the trial, just over 3,500 adults age 50 and older were randomized to receive VAX-31, Prevnar, or Capvaxive. Investigators then measured the strength of their antibody responses against different strains.

How Spain's housing crisis has resulted in an early general election
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez confirmed Spain will be heading to the polls on 29 November, after Sanchez's Socialist party, which is currently heading a minority government, failed to pass housing reforms in the Spanish Congress.
Sanchez faces an uphill battle in his bid for re-election with polls showing Sánchez's Socialist party is trailing the conservative People's Party - which many expect to attempt to form a government with the far-right Vox.
In his statement announcing the election, Sanchez warned Spaniards about what he called the "extreme-right wave" being seen in other countries and said Spain should continue to be a global example of "peace, feminism and prosperity".
BBC correspondent Guy Hedgecoe reports.

INDIA bloc MPs, including Leaders of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, on Tuesday marched from the Parliament House complex towards the Election Commission of India but were stopped by police on Parliament Street, where they sat on a dharna demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
The MPs were stopped in front of the NITI Aayog office, on the stretch between NITI Aayog and Akashvani Bhavan leading towards the Election Commission headquarters.
After being prevented from proceeding further, they sat on the road in protest. Opposition MPs carried cutouts depicting Mr. Kumar in an RSS uniform and raised slogans, including “BJP hai CEC hai”, “Vote chor, gaddi chhod” and “Democracy not for sale”.
In a post on X, Mr. Gandhi posted, “Gyanesh it's done bro. Time to resign".
TMC leaders Abhishek Banerjee, Derek O Brien, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and CPI (M) leader John Brittas were among those who took part in the march
Heavy security deployment and barricading had been put in place in and around Parliament and the Election Commission headquarters ahead of the march.
Security personnel were stationed in the area much before the MPs began arriving. The MPs gathered at Parliament's Makar Dwar before setting off towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission of India headquarters.
Ahead of the march, opposition MPs questioned the security arrangements and stepped up their demand for Mr. Kumar's resignation, citing the Supreme Court's observations on changes to Form 6, the statutory application for enrolment as a voter. Congress MP Imran Masood accused Kumar of eroding public trust in the Election Commission of India.
"Across the country, the institution that Gyanesh Kumar headed was an institution the entire country trusted, an institution the entire country took pride in and felt proud of. Questions were never raised over its impartiality. One person has broken that trust," he told PTI Videos.
"And an entire nexus is working together. We will question Gyanesh Kumar, and the BJP Chief Ministers will start giving the answers," he alleged.
CPI MP P. Sandosh Kumar said the Supreme Court's observations on Monday (October 5, 2026) had strengthened the opposition's objections to the additional declaration attached to Form 6 during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
"On September 26, there was a press statement by the Commission and it was stated that the entire process related to Form 6 has been ratified by the Supreme Court. Whereas it has been proven that it is an entirely misleading statement," he alleged. Calling the CEC a "Cheating Election Commissioner", the CPI leader said opposition parties had been agitating against the provisions since 2025 and would intensify their movement.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut questioned the scale of security deployment ahead of the march, saying the MPs intended to proceed peacefully.
"We are MPs. We are members of Parliament. We are also citizens of this country. Why is there a need to deploy such a large force to stop us? We will walk and go. We are unarmed," he said.
Mr. Raut claimed that Border Security Force and CISF personnel had been deployed and security outside ministers' residences increased.
Accusing Mr. Kumar of misleading the public over the Supreme Court's position on Form 6, he said the CEC had "no moral right" to continue in office.
The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 and would examine the Election Commission's records to ascertain whether changes had been made and who had authorised them.
The observations were made while hearing a petition challenging alleged unilateral decisions by Mr. Kumar.
In its September 26 statement, the Commission had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court, while forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, would be used outside the SIR period.
The protest comes amid an opposition campaign over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise and reports of differences within the three-member Commission. The poll body has rejected suggestions of a split and maintained that decisions relating to SIR were taken unanimously.

Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
Ambani is the son of India’s richest person, Mukesh Ambani, who made his fortune primarily in oil and gas, owns the world’s largest oil refinery and has close ties with the ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP). Mukesh Ambani has enthusiastically praised BJP policies, and firms linked to his Reliance conglomerate have recently made significant donations to the party. The prime minister, Narendra Modi, attended Anant Ambani’s lavish 2024 wedding in Mumbai.
Anant Amabani, 31, who is leads on renewable energy on the Reliance Group’s executive board and is worth an estimated £90bn, has set up Vantara, a 1,400-hectare (3,500-acre) private zoo near the family’s oil refining facilities in Gujarat, which reportedly has more than 150,000 animals including 200 lions, 250 leopards and 900 crocodiles, and where he hosted his opulent pre-wedding celebrations attended by celebrity guests and politicians.
Conservation groups have previously raised questions about how some of the animals were sourced, given many were endangered species. Vantara has never been found guilty of any wrongdoing.
The university’s announcement was met with incredulity and derision from academic staff and Indian and international conservationists and environmentalists.
Ramachandra Guha, a leading Indian public intellectual and the author of the book Speaking With Nature: The Origins of Indian Environmentalism, said: “I must say that it is a rather mystifying choice. As a scholar of Indian and global environmentalism, I can name at least 50 – perhaps 100 – individuals who are far better qualified to be thus honoured. They include soil scientists, energy scientists, water conservation experts, community forest workers, ecologists, pollution abatement experts etc who have made real and tangible contributions to a more sustainable future for India and Indians.
“I wonder on whose advice Newcastle University has acted, and whether it did due diligence on what has and has not been done in these fields. Its appointment of Mr Ambani is puzzling in the extreme, and is likely to adversely affect the university’s institutional credibility and intellectual standing.”
Bhuvan Mangalore, an Indian investigator into illegal wildlife trade who is completing a dissertation on Vantara at Anglia Ruskin University, asked: “Is this a joke?”
Prof Matt Perry, the chair of the University and College Union branch at Newcastle University, said staff members had objected to the appointment citing environmental concerns.
Prof Lyla Mehta, the head of the climate, environment and sustainability department at the University of Sussex’s Institute of Development Studies, shared concerns that “as public funding for universities falls, there is a real danger that billionaire and corporate money begins to shape academia”.
She said: “Universities are supposed to be places that question power and hold corporations to account, not give them academic legitimacy.”
In April, Anant Ambani launched Vantara University, billed as the world’s first global university dedicated to wildlife conservation and veterinary science.
Lorne Stockman, a research co-director at Oil Change International, said: “At a time when the climate crisis demands an urgent phaseout of oil and gas, we must demand our publicly funded institutions do better.”
In 2025, an investigation by the German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung found that many animals delivered to Vantara arrived through countries with opaque wildlife trading networks such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the United Arab Emirates, raising concerns that endangered species may have been illegally trafficked.
In August last year, an investigation by India’s supreme court, which lasted less than three weeks, cleared the zoo’s operators of any wrongdoing. A subsequent fact-finding mission into the zoo by Cites, the UN body that regulates the trade of endangered species, found that some of the permits used to bring animals to Vantara were probably forged.
Its report said: “There is a need for caution to ensure that imports of large numbers of animals by these facilities are not inadvertently creating a demand for illegally sourced animals.”
Cites recommended restrictions on India’s imports of endangered wild animals. However, it subsequently reversed its decision after objections from India, the US and Japan at a Cites meeting after they argued there was not enough proof of illegal imports.
In August, the zoo launched a “reset” in its operations by appointing a former Cites head to oversee its operations and said it would voluntarily pause all wildlife imports until June next year.
Vantara has declined to comment. The Ambani family and Vantara have previously denied the allegations of wildlife trafficking. They have said: “Our mission and focus continues to be the rescue, rehabilitation and care of animals.”
A Newcastle University spokesperson said: “The award of a professorship of practice recognises Mr Ambani’s contributions to conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship through his work with Vantara, a wildlife rescue and conservation initiative, and as the executive lead for the Reliance Group’s transition toward a green energy future.”

The disclosure of BJP’s West Bengal election expenditure has sparked a storm on social media after revealing a Rs 2.5 lakh payment to Bengali actor and vlogger Sayak Chakraborty, who was involved in a controversial beef-steak incident at Kolkata’s Olypub in January 2026.
The report, published on the party’s letterhead and signed by office secretary at the BJP headquarters Mahendra Kumar Pandey details the party’s expenditure between March 15, the date of announcement of West Bengal assembly elections, and May 6, 2026, the official completion of the polls. The report shows that the BJP paid Rs 2,50,000 to a person named Sayak Chakraborty.
The payment appears under Schedule 3, titled “Expense(s) on Media Advertisement (print and electronic, bulk SMS, cable, website and TV channel etc.) on General Party propaganda authorised/incurred by Party Central Headquarters”. Chakraborty is listed at serial number 23 under the “electronic media” category.
The disclosure has drawn particular attention because Chakraborty was involved in a beef-related controversy at the iconic Park Street pub, Olypub, on January 30, 2026.
Following the publication of the expenditure report, Chakraborty acknowledged that he had been paid by the BJP, but claimed it had nothing to do with the Olypub incident.
The Olypub Incident & Why the Expenditure Disclosure Raises Eyebrows
On January 30, Chakraborty alleged that he had been served beef steak instead of a mutton dish at the restaurant. He subsequently lodged an FIR against Olypub and the concerned waiter who allegedly served him beef.
Sayak recorded the heated interaction on a live video and posted it on his Facebook page. His page, ‘Sayakk’, has 1.5 million followers. The 3-minute-47-second video has since been deleted from the page but remains available across social media. The clip can be watched here:
According to Chakraborty, while having dinner at Olypub, he and two friends ordered a mutton steak. The server placed a plate of food on their table without telling them what it was. Unaware of what they had been served, they ate it. After they had finished the dish, the waiter returned with another plate and said, “This is your mutton steak.” When they questioned him about the earlier dish, the waiter allegedly said it had been a beef steak.
Trouble started after that.
In the viral video, Chakraborty can be heard saying, “I ordered mutton steak; how could you mess it up and serve me beef instead? How could you hear beef instead of mutton? Do you know I am a Brahmin? I ate beef instead of mutton because of you!”
He also asked the server, Nasimuddin Sheikh, about his religion, before saying, “You made me eat Go-Mata!”
Following the altercation with the server, the actor lodged an FIR at Park Street police station. Kolkata Police arrested Nasimuddin based on the complaint. He was released on bail four days later.
The disclosure of the BJP’s expenditure immediately raised questions about whether Chakraborty had been paid by the party for his role in the Olypub episode. The questions gained further significance given that the incident had the potential to fuel a communal debate around beef, religion and Hindu identity — ideas that could serve the BJP’s broader political messaging.
They also arose because the immediate relatives of another person who was with Sayak during the incident appear in the BJP’s expenditure list.
At Olypub, while the beef controversy was unfolding, Sayak was accompanied by fellow social media influencer Sukanta Kundu and Kundu’s female friend. The BJP’s list includes the names of Sikha Kundu and Subrata Kundu, identified as Sukanta’s parents. Sikha and Subrata were paid Rs 4,50,000 and Rs 3,00,000 respectively.
Sayak Chakraborty’s Disclosure
As social media posts questioning Chakraborty’s association with the BJP gained traction, and media reports on the issue emerged, Sayak made a Facebook post on the morning of September 26, admitting that he had received a payment from the party.
He, however, claimed that his reaction at Olypub was a genuine outburst and not paid promotion.
He pointed to Olypub’s statement apologising for the meat mix-up as evidence that the episode was not scripted to evoke emotions. According to him, the BJP and others who shared his views simply supported him after the incident.
Chakraborty said the BJP and a few other political parties had subsequently approached him to make promotional content. He accepted the BJP’s offer and made several videos, including content on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), possible reasons behind Narendra Modi’s silence during the conflict, and a congratulatory message for Suvendu Adhikari after he became chief minister.
He reiterated that these videos were made between March and May, the period covered by the BJP’s expenditure report, while the Olypub incident took place in January. Alt News tried calling up Chakraborty on his mobile number, but his phone was switched off.
Kundu, too, shared a Facebook post on September 26, acknowledging that the payment details being linked to him were indeed genuine. At the same time, he asserted that the Olypub incident was not part of his political campaign.

Confession: When BougeRV told me about its remote-controlled wagon with animated lighting, I called it in for a laugh, expecting to eviscerate it in a review. It’s ridiculous, to be sure. But the DuneRover also proved very capable, with enough torque to flatten hills even when carrying over 200 pounds of gear. It can also traverse soft sand that defeats conventional wagons.
This remote-controlled wagon is silly but so very useful
BougeRV’s DuneRover is so good on hills and sand that you’ll forgive the disco lights.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
As someone who regularly uses a variety of wagons to haul all sorts of gear, the DuneRover is an epiphany. But what BougeRV sent me was a Kickstarter prototype — and it shows.
Production units won’t ship until February 2027. So, what follows is less of a review and more a risk assessment for those considering backing the Kickstarter. That way, you can decide whether it makes sense to lock down early-bird pricing at $467, a claimed 48 percent discount off the eventual $899 list price. (Though I’ll wager it’ll always be sold for some kind of discount.)
Frankly, $500 isn’t outlandish for a wagon. Prices start at around $40 for a rickety model that will only last a few months, $300 for something durable from a reputable brand, and closer to $800 at the top end. And none of those wagons provides a motorized assist.
Let’s begin with the dumb stuff. The wagon has LED light bars on the back that are on by default and could come in handy at a campsite after dark. You can turn them off via the app, but you have to do it every time you restart the wagon. The default for a battery-powered device used primarily during the day should obviously be off.
Then there’s the remote control. I think I know what happened here. The product designers had a choice: route a cable through all the folding mechanisms that separate the motor from the handle or make it wireless. Wireless won, and then someone from marketing said, ‘Hey, I’ve got an idea!’
I mean, a remote-controlled wagon is so absurd that it’s kind of fun, and it brought a lot of joyful finger-pointing to onlookers during my testing. Maybe that’s enough?
The DuneRover is no joke for hauling gear. It’s fitted with two brushless geared motors, each producing up to 400W of output and up to 33Nm of torque. The wagon is activated by a trigger embedded in the handle that you press naturally when you pull the cart. Walk faster and the wagon will roll faster. Sometimes the wagon will lurch forward on that initial pull before settling into your walking rhythm. It’s not dangerous, it’s just unexpected. Release the trigger on the handle, and the wagon stops, even on an incline.
Pulling an oversized load weighing over 200 pounds up a 10 percent grade required a modicum of effort — but just a tenth of what it would have taken without the motor assist. Even on that steep incline, the wagon stops (with an inch or two of rollback) just as soon as I let go of the trigger. Repeated stopping and starting on slopes did, however, seem to confuse the DuneRover, occasionally causing the motors to become jerky as soon as I started walking again. A simple on/off resumed normal operation.
The motors also regulate speed when walking downhill with a heavy load. With the trigger held down, the controller did a good job monitoring changes in acceleration and countering the wagon’s speed to maintain my walking pace. When I stopped, so did the wagon, even on that 10 percent grade with a 200-plus pound load.
The motors aren’t powerful enough to haul that same load through soft sand, however. The oversized beach wheels performed much better in sand with loads weighing about half that, and should be excellent for families carrying a cooler, snacks, beach umbrella, toddler, and toys for a day at the beach.
I like that the DuneRover easily transformed depending on what I needed to haul. The sides can be unzipped and folded flat to convert the wagon into a cart for hauling oversized items or a senior dog. You can also unzip the sides but leave the straps connected to create more volume inside the wagon. I used this configuration a lot. Just know that you’ll want to bring a few bungee cords or cargo nets to keep everything securely in place.
My prototype suffered from intermittent rolling resistance with the motor off. The wagon would roll along fine for five or six feet, but then the wheels attached to the motors would brake, drag along the ground, and then release after a second or two. BougeRV assures me this isn’t something that would be exhibited by its production wagons. I ended up just leaving the motor on throughout my testing, even when I didn’t need it. The 82.14Wh battery was more than up to the challenge.
I used the DuneRover to move gear out of a beach house along the same route where I tested BougeRV’s original electric wagon. Six times I pulled the DuneRover along a path with 5 percent grade on one end and a 10 percent grade on the other. After six kilometers (3.73 miles) of soft sand, hard asphalt, wooden ramps, and gravel, the battery still showed a 74 percent charge. Not bad.
The removable battery features a bi-directional 100W USB-C port, making it a rather capable power bank. It can also charge from a 100W solar panel plugged into its XT-60 jack, thanks to a built-in MPPT solar controller. The battery in my prototype is not protected against rain, so I tested it in dry conditions, though BougeRV promises “full-vehicle IPX6-rated protection” in the production wagon.
The DuneRover is a beast at 59.5 pounds (27kg) with the battery and wheels installed. It’s also rather chunky when it folds. The quick-release front wheels can be removed if a flatter pack is required.
Overall, I’m impressed with the prototype DuneRover I tested — it’s capable, versatile, and proved to be an enormous help over the last few weeks of moving things between a holiday home, home, and adventure van. Like most BougeRV products, it gets the basics right, but not without a few annoyances and inconveniences. I’d expect the same from whatever ships to Kickstarter backers early next year.

Samoa prime minister apologizes for Nazi gesture and saying 'Heil Hitler' in 2007 video
Samoa’s Prime Minister Laʻauli Leuatea Schmidt has apologized for a 2007 video that showed him saying “Heil Hitler” and making a Nazi gesture
WELLINGTON, New Zealand -- Samoa’s Prime Minister Laʻauli Leuatea Schmidt apologized Monday for a video from 19 years earlier in which he said “Heil Hitler” and made a Nazi gesture during what he described as a family gathering.
His statement published on the government's Facebook page came a day after the Samoa Observer newspaper made public for the first time the existence and content of a seven-second clip that the outlet said was filmed at a Schmidt family reunion in Samoa in July 2007.
In a screenshot from the video, Schmidt holds a microphone in one hand with the other arm lifted, surrounded by others making the same gesture.
The newspaper reported Schmidt was heard saying into the microphone, “Raise your right hand, Heil Hitler!”
Schmidt, who was the deputy speaker of Samoa's Parliament in 2007, didn't dispute the report. He has led the South Pacific island nation of 220,000 people since winning an August 2025 election.
“I recognise that those words and gesture were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt and I apologise for using them,” he said Monday. He added that the video was filmed “at a private family gathering — not intended for the public.”
He rejected “Nazism, antisemitism, racism and all forms of political extremism,” the statement said.
What happened immediately before and after the moment depicted was unknown, the newspaper said, and Schmidt's statement didn't explain further.
The episode unfolded as Pacific media groups decried Schmidt's ongoing rancor against the Observer, which has been barred from covering his and other government news conferences and events since November, when Schmidt accused the newspaper of misleading coverage.
On Friday, Schmidt confirmed claims that an Observer reporter's photos of him, taken in front of government buildings during an official event, were deleted from their camera by an aide. He defended the move, saying the Observer, Samoa's largest newspaper group, was flouting its prohibition.
The Observer has called his ban “authoritarian.” Pacific media groups have called on the prime minister for a reversal, with the Journalists Association of Samoa saying it was “deeply disturbed” by the photo deletion incident.
Like a number of other leaders of small island nations in the South Pacific Ocean, Schmidt has voiced vehement support for Israel before.
Since September 2023, three Pacific islands, not including Samoa, have been among a handful of countries to follow the United States in opening embassies in the contested city of Jerusalem instead of Tel Aviv, where most diplomatic missions are located.
Analysts attribute support for Israel in the region to deep Christian traditions woven throughout public life. When Schmidt was sworn into office in September 2025, he wore a Jewish prayer shawl during a ceremony that included the blowing of a shofar.
“Samoa will not withdraw from supporting Israel as the country of God’s people,” he told reporters after the event, according to local news outlets.

Throughout music history, there have been plenty of record-breaking songs, albums, and acts.
These 13, however, have seen the most success on the Billboard Hot 100, which is widely considered to be the definitive ranking of best-selling songs in the US.
Keep scrolling to see the elite tier of singles artists, listed from least to most No. 1 hits.
11 (tie). Bruno Mars — 10
Mars earned his 10th No. 1 single — and his first song to debut at No. 1 — in January 2026 with "I Just Might."
This comes 16 years after his first chart-topper, "Nothin' on You," in May 2016. Then came: "Just the Way You Are" also in 2010, "Grenade" in 2011, "Locked Out of Heaven" in 2012, "When I Was Your Man" in 2013, "Uptown Funk!" in 2015, "That's What I Like" in 2017, "Leave the Door Open" in 2021, and "Die With a Smile" in 2025.
11 (tie). Stevie Wonder — 10
In 1963, at just 13 years old, Stevie Wonder earned his first No. 1 song with "Fingertips." He was the youngest artist ever to top the chart.
Throughout his illustrious career, Wonder has added nine more hits to the list: "Superstition" in 1972, "You Are the Sunshine of My Life" in 1973, "You Haven't Done Nothin'" in 1974, "I Wish" in 1976, "Sir Duke" in 1977, "Ebony and Ivory" in 1982, "I Just Called to Say I Love You" in 1984, and both "Part-Time Lover" and "That's What Friends Are For" in 1985.
11 (tie). Janet Jackson — 10
Janet Jackson's reign on the Hot 100 began with 1986's "When I Think of You," which topped the chart when she was 20 years old.
Next came 1989's "Miss You Much," 1990's "Escapade," "Black Cat," and "Love Will Never Do (Without You)," 1993's "That's the Way Love Goes" and "Again," 1997's "Together Again," 2000's "Doesn't Really Matter," and 2001's "All for You."
Jackson is the rare artist to claim the No. 1 spot in three different decades, like Stevie Wonder.
10. Whitney Houston — 11
Whitney Houston had no shortage of iconic songs, but she earned her first No. 1 with "Saving All My Love for You" in 1985. That same year, she also put "How Will I Know" in the top spot.
Over the next decade, Houston collected nine more chart-toppers: "The Greatest Love of All" in 1986; "I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me)," "Didn't We Almost Have It All," and "So Emotional" in 1987; "Where Do Broken Hearts Go" in 1988; "I'm Your Baby Tonight" and "All the Man That I Need" in 1990; "I Will Always Love You" in 1992; and "Exhale (Shoop Shoop)" in 1995.
8 (tie). Madonna — 12
Madonna has been topping the charts for decades, and it all began with "Like a Virgin" in 1984.
She followed up with "Crazy for You" in 1985 before she scored three No. 1 hits in 1986 alone: "Live to Tell," "Papa Don't Preach," and "Open Your Heart."
The so-called "Queen of Pop" added to her collection with "Who's That Girl" in 1987, "Like a Prayer" in 1989, "Vogue" and "Justify My Love" in 1990, "This Used to Be My Playground" in 1992, "Take a Bow" in 1994, and "Music" in 2000.
8 (tie). The Supremes — 12
The Supremes are known as one of the best-selling girl groups of all time, earning 12 No. 1 hits in half as many years.
In the mid-'60s, the trio released a string of five singles that all went to No. 1 on the chart: "Where Did Our Love Go," "Baby Love," and "Come See About Me" in 1964, then "Stop! In the Name of Love" and "Back in My Arms Again" in 1965.
They continued to dominate the decade with a flood of hits: "I Hear a Symphony," also in 1965; "You Can't Hurry Love" and "You Keep Me Hangin' On" in 1966; "Love Is Here and Now You're Gone" and "The Happening" in 1967; "Love Child" in 1968; and "Someday We'll Be Together" in 1969.
7. Michael Jackson — 13
Michael Jackson began appearing on the charts as a child with The Jackson 5, but after he struck out on his own, the so-called "King of Pop" racked up more hits than any solo artist at the time.
Perhaps most impressively, five out of his 13 No. 1 songs came from the same album ("Bad"), setting a record that remains unbroken. (It was tied in 2011 by Katy Perry's "Teenage Dream.")
Jackson's first chart-topper was "Ben" in 1972 when he was 14 years old. "Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough" and "Rock With You" both took the top spot in 1979, followed by "Billie Jean," "Beat It," and "Say Say Say" in 1983; "I Just Can't Stop Loving You," "Bad," and "The Way You Make Me Feel" in 1987; "Man in the Mirror" and "Dirty Diana" in 1988; and "Black or White" in 1993.
He capped his collection with "You Are Not Alone" in 1995, which also became the first song in history to debut at No. 1 on the Hot 100.
5 (tie). Drake — 14
Drake is one of the most dominant artists of the streaming era, racking up 14 chart-topping singles to date — the vast majority of them at breakneck speed over a seven-year period.
The rapper notched his first No. 1 hit thanks to Rihanna when their collaboration, "What's My Name," reigned atop the chart in 2010.
In 2016, Drake topped the chart again as a featured artist on Rihanna's song "Work." Later that year, "One Dance" became his first solo hit to ascend to first place.
He notched three No. 1 hits in 2018 with "God's Plan," "Nice for What," and "In My Feelings," followed by "Toosie Slide" in 2020; "What's Next" and "Way 2 Sexy" in 2021; "Wait for U" and "Jimmy Cooks" in 2022; "Slime You Out" and "First Person Shooter" in 2023; and "Janice STFU" in 2026.
Ten of those songs arrived in the chart's top spot, making Drake the artist with the most No. 1 song debuts in history.
5 (tie). Rihanna — 14
In the span of just 14 years, Rihanna earned 14 No. 1 songs, starting with "SOS" in 2006 when she was still a teenager.
Next came "Umbrella" in 2007; "Take a Bow," "Live Your Life," and "Disturbia" in 2008; "Rude Boy," "Love the Way You Lie," "Only Girl (In the World)," and "What's My Name" in 2010; "S&M" and "We Found Love" in 2011; "Diamonds" in 2012; "The Monster" in 2013; and finally "Work" in 2016, the lead single from her most recent album, "Anti."
4. Taylor Swift — 16
Taylor Swift's first No. 1 hit was "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" in 2012. It was released as the lead single from Swift's fourth album, "Red."
Swift's fifth album, "1989," spawned three No. 1 singles: "Shake It Off" and "Blank Space" in 2014, followed by the "Bad Blood" remix featuring Kendrick Lamar in 2015.
"Look What You Made Me Do" became her fifth chart leader in 2017, followed by "Cardigan" and "Willow" in 2020.
In 2021, Swift launched her series of rerecorded albums, sending an extended version of an old deep cut, "All Too Well," to the top of the chart. At 10 minutes and 13 seconds, it's the longest No. 1 hit in Billboard history.
In her "Midnights" era, Swift's 2022 single "Anti-Hero" topped the chart for eight weeks.
In 2023, Swift notched her milestone 10th No. 1 with "Cruel Summer," fueled by the success of the Eras Tour. Shortly after, "Is It Over Now?" and "Fortnight" joined the ranks.
"The Fate of Ophelia," the lead single from "The Life of a Showgirl," became Swift's 13th leader and her biggest No. 1 hit to date, topping the chart for 10 weeks.
The album's second single, "Opalite," topped the chart dated February 28, thanks to a unique strategy that kept the music video exclusive to Spotify and Apple Music, and off YouTube (since YouTube views no longer count toward the charts).
In 2026, "I Knew It, I Knew You" and "Patient Zero" became her 15th and 16th No. 1s, putting her behind only Elvis Presley, Mariah Carey, and The Beatles.
Notably, Swift is credited as the lead cowriter on all of her No. 1 songs.
3. Elvis Presley — 18
Technically, some of Elvis Presley's career predated the Hot 100, which was launched in 1958. But he topped its predecessor, the pop chart, and the Hot 100 a combined total of 18 times.
In 1956, his No. 1 singles were: "Heartbreak Hotel," "I Want You, I Need You, I Love You," "Don't Be Cruel," "Hound Dog," and "Love Me Tender."
The next year, 1957, he released the chart-toppers "Too Much," "All Shook Up," "(Let Me Be Your) Teddy Bear," and "Jailhouse Rock."
In 1958, there was "Don't" and "Hard Headed Woman," while in 1959, there was "A Big Hunk o' Love."
The '60s were slower for the King of Rock 'n' Roll. He had the No. 1s "Stuck on You," "Now or Never,' and "Are You Lonesome Tonight," in 1960; "Surrender" in 1961; "Good Luck Charm" in 1962; and his final No. 1, "Suspicious Minds," in 1969.
2. Mariah Carey — 19
In terms of No. 1 songs, Mariah Carey is the second-best-selling artist of all time, the best-selling solo artist of all time, and the best-selling female artist of all time.
Her first No. 1 hit was also her debut single, 1990's "Vision of Love." Her next four singles would also top the chart: "Love Takes Time" in 1990, followed by "Someday," "I Don't Wanna Cry," and "Emotions" in 1991.
Then came a veritable feast of hit songs: "I'll Be There" in 1992; "Dreamlover" and "Hero" in 1993; "Fantasy" and "One Sweet Day" in 1995; "Always Be My Baby" in 1996; "Honey" in 1997; "My All" in 1998; "Heartbreaker" in 1999; "Thank God I Found You" in 2000; "We Belong Together" and "Don't Forget About Us" in 2005; and "Touch My Body" in 2008.
In 2020, she became the first and only artist in history to top the Billboard Hot 100 in four different decades, thanks to the longevity of her 1994 holiday single "All I Want for Christmas Is You."
1. The Beatles — 20
The Beatles still reign supreme with the most No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200 and the most No. 1 songs on the Hot 100, earning 20 in just eight years.
In chronological order, the British band topped the chart with "Love Me Do" in 1962; "She Loves You" and "I Want to Hold Your Hand" in 1963; "Can't Buy Me Love," "A Hard Day's Night," and "I Feel Fine" in 1964; "Eight Days a Week," "Ticket to Ride," "Help!," "Yesterday," and "We Can Work It Out" in 1965; "Paperback Writer" in 1966; "Penny Lane" "All You Need Is Love," and "Hello, Goodbye" in 1967; "Hey Jude" in 1968; "Get Back" and "Something" in 1969; and "Let It Be" and "The Long and Winding Road" in 1970.
The band's most recent song, "Now and Then," peaked at No. 7 on the chart and won best rock performance at the 2024 Grammy Awards.

'Rock, paper, scissors' decides London Marathon dates
- Published
A game of rock, paper, scissors was used to determine when the elite female and male races will take place during next year's unique two-day London Marathon.
After confirming they were playing for the right to race on the traditional Sunday, women's wheelchair world record holder Catherine Debrunner beat men's world record holder Sabastian Sawe - both 2026 London Marathon champions in their respective races - in the contest.
As a result, the elite men and men's wheelchair races are set for Saturday, 24 April, with the women's races the following day.
Hugh Brasher, chief executive of London Marathon Events, said: "Sabastian and Catherine's rock, paper, scissors battle was an entertaining way to decide which day would host each elite race.
"Splitting the elite races will allow us to shine an even brighter spotlight on the extraordinary athletes taking part."
Earlier this year, organisers of the event confirmed the London Marathon will be held across two days in what is said to be a momentous one-off edition of the event.
The decision was made to enable more people to take part, after a record 1.33 million people entered the ballot for next year.
In 2027 a record-breaking 100,000 participants will take part and it is estimated that more than £150m will be raised for charitable causes.
The women's championship categories will line-up behind the women's elite field for the first time in the London race.
"Our outstanding elite women's wheelchair field will begin the action just ahead of them, creating a true celebration of women's marathon racing," Brasher added.
The main events on both days will be a mixed field of male, female and non-binary participants.

India had the highest number of children with no sanitation service in schools, with 50 million out of the world total of 244 million as of 2025, according to a new global report. Only Nigeria (34 million), Ethiopia (26 million), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (11 million) or Indonesia (8 million) had a comparatively large number of schoolchildren who had no access to sanitation service.
The data from ‘Progress on drinking water, sanitation and hygiene in schools 2015-2025’ shows the progress as well as the challenges India is facing in meeting the water, sanitation and hygiene goals that are part of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) set for 2030.
14% reduction in schools with no sanitation service
The report can also be seen as a decadal report card on the Swachh Bharat Mission, which was launched in India on October 2, 2014. The report cites the achievement of India which saw a 14% reduction in schools with no sanitation service.
Lack of hygiene service
The WHO/UNICEF report that is part of the Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) shows that globally, 362 million children still had no hygiene service at their school in 2025. Of these, 20 million were from India.
It is not just lack of access that the WHO report flags about India but also gaps in data. “There is now sufficient data to estimate trends in basic hygiene coverage between 2015 and 2025 for all SDG regions except Central and Southern Asia where there were insufficient recent data to generate estimates for India, and therefore the region, beyond 2024.”
Drinking water
On the brighter side, India is among the 28 out of 62 countries that are on track to achieve universal coverage of basic drinking water in schools by 2030.
As of 2025, there were 258 million children who still had no drinking water service at their school. The number of children from Indian schools made up 12 million of this number or about 1 out 20 children in the world. The report shows that India has made a big progress in basic drinking water services in 2025 and average rates of change between 2015 and 2025. India, Panama, Syrian Arab Republic, Togo and Tuvalu increased coverage by over 4% per year, “demonstrating that rapid progress is possible”.
However, the report found that while gaps in basic water coverage persists between school levels and between rural and urban areas, this did not apply to India, Cambodia and Fiji.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in September, held a secret meeting with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the President of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The meeting came against the backdrop of Tel Aviv's strained ties with several Arab countries over its military offensive in Gaza and subsequent actions in Lebanon. The meeting between Netanyahu and MBZ is now raising questions about Israel's ties with its Arab neighbours, particularly as the third anniversary of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack approaches. Following Hamas' attack, the war that ensued caused widespread destruction in Gaza and affected Israel's relations with not just its Arab neighbours but other countries as well. 1. UAE: The latest meeting between Netanyahu and MBZ reportedly centered around bilateral ties, with Abu Dhabi acknowledging the meeting for the first time on Monday, 28 September. According to a recent statement, the UAE government said that, after the meeting, the two sides have maintained open and direct lines of communication since the relationship began in 2020. The statement added that whenever necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities. According to a Reuters report, in 2020, the UAE surprised many Arab states by agreeing to normalize ties with Tel Aviv under US President Donald Trump's 'Abraham Accords.' The agreement enabled the UAE and Israel to strengthen cooperation in addressing what both viewed as security threats from Shi'ite Iran and Sunni Islamist groups. The normaliztion was also intended to support efforts towards the establishment of a Palestinian state, an objective that has come under pressure following the war in Gaza. 2. Egypt: Egypt and Israel fought wars in 1948, 1956, 1967 and 1973, but the two sides struck the first peace deal between Israel and its Arab neighbour in 1978 at Camp David. According to a Reuters report, while Tel Aviv and Cairo cooperate on oil and gas, they have little other trade. However, the ties have been strained since the Gaza war. In December last year, Badr Abdelatty, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Immigration, and Egyptian Expatriate Affairs, stressed that any displacement of Palestinians remains a “red line” for Egypt, adding that the Rafah crossing would not be used to facilitate any forced or voluntary displacement plan. Egypt, he said, would neither participate in nor support such efforts. 3. Jordan: Jordan, like Egypt, has a peace deal with Israel since 1994 and is the Arab state with the closest ties to Palestinians. However, anger over Tel Aviv's treatment of Palestinians has been widespread in Jordan and was sharpened by the war in Gaza. 4. Bahrain: Bahrain normalized ties with Israel after the UAE, and the two maintain formal diplomatic relations under the Abraham Accords of 2020. 5. Saudi Arabia: While Saudi Arabia has always presented itself as a supporter of the Palestinian cause, it has kept the door open to future ties with Israel. In 2000, it rallied other Arab countries behind the Arab Peace Initiative, which proposed full diplomatic normalization with Israel in exchange for the establishment of a Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital and a resolution to the issue of Palestinian refugees. In August, in a joint statement with the ministers of foreign affairs of the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt, Riyadh condemned Israel’s continued illegal settlement policies in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and rejected the “E1” settlement plan and related settlement activities east of occupied East Jerusalem. While there seem to be no diplomatic relations between the two sides, in September, Israel signalled that it is prepared to take action against Iran-backed Houthis and support Saudi Arabia, but the Kingdom did not indicate intent to seek Tel Aviv's assistance. 6. Oman: According to The Israel Times, Oman does not have diplomatic ties with Israel. While the two countries once maintained commercial relations, those ties were strained in 2000 and eventually cut as the Israeli-Palestinian conflict worsened. However, contacts between the two countries continued quietly later, with Netanyahu visiting Oman in 2018 in a rare public meeting; as of 2026, the ties have not been restored to normalcy, particularly after the 7 October attack and Tel Aviv's actions in Gaza. 7. Syria: Syria does not have diplomatic relations or a peace treaty with Israel, and the two have been in a state of war. During the 1967 war, Israel seized much of Syria's Golan Heights. Under the rule of the Assad family, relations between Damascus and Tel Aviv entered a period of open hostility. Earlier in August, Reuters reported that the two sides held US-mediated talks to ease tensions. 8. Lebanon: Lebanon does not have any diplomatic relations with Israel. SEOUL – South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks and called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era.
“In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used, causing considerable public concern and anxiety,” Lee said during a cabinet meeting.
“Please establish the circumstances swiftly and clearly, and concentrate personnel and resources on minimizing the damage.”
South Korea’s police have launched a full-scale investigation into the hacking attacks against commercial banks that led to a breach of customers’ personal information, the Yonhap news agency reported on Tuesday.
Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, the Financial Services Commission (FSC) said on Friday, while Yonhap reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank also suffered breaches.
Authorities have not yet disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used in the hacking incidents or the full scale of the breaches.
On Sunday, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance.
Financial watchdog the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Financial Security Institute shared data about 28 unique IP addresses and some country information linked to the recent hacking attempts with the financial sector, the FSS said on Tuesday.
In September, Australia said an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorized access to files, in what could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website.
An artificial intelligence research firm said last week that AI agents tried to hack into a Canadian government website, casting the effort as a failed hacking attempt, while Canada said there were no indications its systems were compromised.
