Casey Bloys‘ new role at a new company comes with a new contract too. Deadline has confirmed that Bloys, named earlier today Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC, has signed a multi-year extension to his current Warner Bros. Discovery contract, which runs though end of 2027.
Contract renewals are standard practice for hires at that level. Getting a long-term commitment from Bloys was likely part of Paramount — and now Skydance — CEO David Ellison’s decision to go with the decorated HBO executive over Paramount’s DTC Chair Cindy Holland in one of the most dramatic choices he had to make while assembling the top executive suite of the combined company post-WBD merger.
Bloys, who will oversee content for both HBO Max and Paramount+, is expected to take some time and evaluate Holland’s programming team at Paramount+ before making personnel decisions. He is bringing with him his core group of HBO/HBO Max executives, HBO head of drama Francesca Orsi, HBO and HBO Max head of comedy Amy Gravitt, HBO Max head of originals Sarah Aubrey and HBO/HBO Max head of communications Jeff Cusson. Like Bloys, Orsi, Gravitt and Cusson all had been at HBO for more than 20 years.
Watch on Deadline
Bloys, who started at HBO in 2004 as a comedy executive, rose to head of comedy before being named President of Programming in 2016. He added original content responsibilities for HBO Max in 2020 and was named Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content in 2022.
Under his tenure, HBO has remained a powerhouse, generating hit, acclaimed series. HBO/HBO Max is coming off another strong Emmy season, winning 21 awards out of 122 nominations, including Outstanding Drama Series for The Pitt and Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series for DTF St. Louis.
The news of Bloys’ re-up was first reported by the Ankler.

Since releasing her first No. 1 album in 2008, Taylor Swift has enjoyed a historic run on the charts, topping the Billboard 200 and Billboard Hot 100 over a dozen times each.
Swift's collection of chart-toppers includes both radio-friendly pop singles and understated gems pushed to the top of the chart by passionate fans.
Most recently, "Patient Zero" joined the ranks of Swift's biggest songs. On the all-time ranking of most No. 1 hits, Swift only trails Elvis, Mariah Carey, and The Beatles.
All of Swift's No. 1 songs on the Hot 100 are listed below in chronological order of their peak dates.
1. "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together"
Weeks at No. 1: Three
Despite writing ubiquitous hits like "You Belong With Me" and "Love Story" earlier in her career (which peaked at No. 2 and No. 4, respectively), "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" was Swift's first-ever song to top the Hot 100.
The country-pop crossover smash was released as the lead single from Swift's fourth album, "Red." It rose from No. 72 to No. 1 in its second week of tracking and remained atop the chart for two more weeks.
2. "Shake It Off"
Weeks at No. 1: Four
"Shake It Off" was released as the lead single from Swift's fifth album, "1989." It became her first No. 1 debut on the Hot 100.
3. "Blank Space"
Weeks at No. 1: Seven
"Blank Space," the second single from "1989," debuted at No. 18 on the Hot 100.
It rose to No. 13 before soaring to No. 1 in its third week — dethroning "Shake It Off" and making Swift the first woman in history to replace herself in the chart's top spot.
"Blank Space" went on to become one of Swift's biggest hits, reigning atop the chart for nearly two months.
4. "Bad Blood" featuring Kendrick Lamar
Weeks at No. 1: One
In May 2015, a remix of "Bad Blood" featuring Kendrick Lamar was released as the fourth single from "1989."
It rose from No. 53 to the chart's top spot after the music video premiered at the 2015 Billboard Music Awards and broke the Vevo record for most views in 24 hours.
5. "Look What You Made Me Do"
Weeks at No. 1: Three
Despite mixed reactions from critics, Swift's lead single from "Reputation" rose to No. 1 after its first full week of tracking, breaking the weekly streaming record for a song by a woman.
Once again, Swift's music video broke the record for most views within 24 hours, racking up 43.2 million views in its first day.
6. "Cardigan"
Weeks at No. 1: One
Swift announced the arrival of her eighth album, "Folklore," just one day in advance. The second track, "Cardigan," was released alongside the album and promoted with a whimsical music video.
"Folklore" debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 while "Cardigan" simultaneously debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100, making Swift the first artist in history to open atop both charts in the same week.
7. "Willow"
Weeks at No. 1: One
Just five months after "Folklore," Swift repeated her pandemic-era strategy and surprise-released her ninth album, "Evermore," alongside its lead single.
Again, "Willow" debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100 while "Evermore" simultaneously debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
8. "All Too Well (Taylor's Version)"
Weeks at No. 1: One
"Red (Taylor's Version)" was the second rerecorded album Swift released. It was accompanied by the long-awaited 10-minute version of "All Too Well," a fan-favorite track from the original album.
"All Too Well (10 Minute Version) (Taylor's Version)" was promoted with a self-directed short film starring Sadie Sink and Dylan O'Brien, a convention-breaking performance on "Saturday Night Live," and plenty of theories about the song's muse.
It debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100, becoming the longest song in history to top the chart. The record was previously held by Don McLean's "American Pie (Parts I & II)" at 8 minutes and 37 seconds.
9. "Anti-Hero"
Weeks at No. 1: Eight
"Anti-Hero" was released alongside Swift's 10th album, "Midnights," and promoted as the lead single.
It dominated the Hot 100 for eight weeks, surpassing the high-water mark set by "Blank Space."
The same week that "Anti-Hero" debuted at No. 1, Swift became the first and only artist in history to occupy the entire top 10 on the Hot 100. The hit single was flanked by "Lavender Haze" (No. 2), "Maroon" (No. 3), "Snow on the Beach" (No. 4), "Midnight Rain" (No. 5), "Bejeweled" (No. 6), "Question...?" (No. 7), "You're On Your Own, Kid" (No. 8), "Karma" (No. 9), and "Vigilante Shit" (No. 10).
10. "Cruel Summer"
Weeks at No. 1: Four
"Cruel Summer" was originally released as the second track on Swift's 2019 album "Lover."
Although it was identified early as a fan favorite, the song was never promoted as a single and debuted modestly at No. 29 on the Hot 100.
Four years later, Swift transformed "Cruel Summer" into a showstopping spectacle on the Eras Tour. Streams of the song began to surge, and it reigned atop Billboard's Pop Airplay chart for two months. Swift's label sent the song to pop radio in June 2023.
Finally, following the release of "The Cruelest Summer" EP — which includes a live version of the song and a remix by LP Giobbi — the song reached No. 1 on the Hot 100, marking Swift's milestone 10th chart-topper.
11. "Is It Over Now?"
Weeks at No. 1: One
"Is It Over Now?" was released as the final vault track on "1989 (Taylor's Version)," a rerecording of her beloved fifth album.
Although it wasn't initially slated as a single, its enthusiastic reception from fans pushed Swift's team to serve the song to pop radio.
"Is It Over Now?" debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100, dethroning "Cruel Summer." Swift remains the only woman in history to replace herself in the top spot, a feat she's now achieved twice.
12. "Fortnight" featuring Post Malone
Weeks at No. 1: Two
"Fortnight," a duet with Post Malone, was released alongside "The Tortured Poets Department" and promoted as the album's lead single.
The song debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100 while "Poets" simultaneously debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
For the second time in her career, Swift managed to occupy the entire top 10 of the Hot 100. In fact, the top 14 positions on the chart were occupied by "Poets" tracks, including "Down Bad" (No. 2) and "I Can Do It With a Broken Heart" (No. 3), all the way through to "The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived" (No. 14).
"Fortnight" returned to No. 1 on the Hot 100 for a second consecutive week.
13. "The Fate of Ophelia"
Weeks at No. 1: 10
"The Fate of Ophelia" was released alongside Swift's 12th studio album, "The Life of a Showgirl," and promoted as the lead single.
The Shakespeare-inspired pop song debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100, while "Showgirl" simultaneously debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
All 12 tracks on the album debuted within the Hot 100's top 12 spots, making Swift the first and only artist to dominate the chart's entire top 10 on three separate occasions. "The Fate of Ophelia" was joined in the top five by "Opalite" (No. 2), "Elizabeth Taylor" (No. 3), "Father Figure" (No. 4), and "Wood" (No. 5).
"The Fate of Ophelia" remained atop the Hot 100 for eight straight weeks after its release. After falling to lower positions during the holiday season, it returned to No. 1 in early 2026, surpassing "Anti-Hero" as Swift's longest-leading hit to date and becoming her first to top the chart for double-digit weeks.
14. "Opalite"
Weeks at No. 1: One
"Opalite" was originally released as the third track on "The Life of a Showgirl" and debuted at No. 2 on the Hot 100.
It was later promoted as the album's second single, rising to No. 1 after Swift sold vinyl copies of the song. She also released a music video co-starring Domhnall Gleeson, which premiered exclusively on Spotify and Apple Music in a savvy move to boost streaming numbers.
Swift celebrated her latest chart achievement on Instagram, thanking fans for their support of the song.
"This is actually the first time I've had two Hot 100 #1s off of one album since my album 1989 came out in 2014, nearly twelve years ago!" Swift wrote. "I know that's a lot of numbers but it all adds up to me being so thankful to the fans who helped make this happen by welcoming this song into your lives with open arms."
15. "I Knew It, I Knew You"
Weeks at No. 1: Two
"I Knew It, I Knew You" was released as a soundtrack single for Pixar's "Toy Story 5."
The twangy tune, cowritten by Swift and her longtime producer Jack Antonoff, was embraced by country radio and debuted simultaneously at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the Hot Country Songs charts.
16. "Patient Zero"
Weeks at No. 1: One
"Patient Zero" was released as a deluxe track from "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore."
Swift said she was inspired to write more "Showgirl" songs during a trip to visit her Swedish collaborators, Max Martin and Shellback, to celebrate the album's historic first-week sales.
"I hope you love them, because they were born out of pure gratitude for your exuberance for and celebration of the album we made," Swift wrote on social media.
"Patient Zero" followed in the chart-topping footsteps of "The Fate of Ophelia" and "Opalite," making "Showgirl" the first female album to spawn three No. 1 hits since Swift's own "1989" over a decade earlier.

Jim Bakker, who built 'PTL Club' televangelism empire, has died at 86
Jim Bakker, who along with his first wife Tammy Faye built an evangelical empire around the hugely successful "The PTL Club" TV show, only to lose it all over a sex scandal and financial crimes, has died. He was 86.
Bakker died Monday, his second wife, Lori Bakker, said in a statement. His cause of death was not immediately clear.
"He was a pioneer of Christian television, but to me, he was my husband, my best friend, and the man I was honored to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry," she said.
The pair lived near the Missouri entertainment town of Branson and filmed their TV show "The Jim Bakker Show" there since it launched in 2003. Bakker suffered a stroke in 2020.
But it was another evangelical program that made Jim and his first wife Tammy Faye Bakker cultural icons — so much so that they were often skewered in the 1980s and 1990s by late-night comedians and parodied on "Saturday Night Live." A theatrical movie on their lives, "The Eyes of Tammy Faye," was released in September 2021.
At its peak in the mid-1980s, the Bakkers' ministry included not only the TV show drawing up to 13 million nightly viewers but also the Christian-based Heritage USA theme park and hotel in Fort Mill, South Carolina.
Bakker got his start as a traveling preacher
Bakker was born in Muskegon, Michigan, and attended North Central Bible College in Minneapolis, where he met Tammy Faye. They married in 1961 and dropped out of college to start their own traveling ministry — he preached, she sang and played the accordion as they crossed the country visiting churches and tent revivals.
They caught the attention of televangelist Pat Robertson, and in 1965 launched a children's show on Robertson's Christian Broadcasting Network. By 1966, he was hosting "The 700 Club," a Christian talk show.
Bakker left CBN in 1972 and two years later formed the PTL Satellite Network. "The PTL Club" — PTL stands for "Praise the Lord" — became its signature show.
When it hit its heyday in the 1980s, "The PTL Club" was drawing millions of viewers — and bringing in millions of dollars annually from followers.
The show featured chats with guests and Christian entertainers. Bakker offered upbeat sermons and Tammy Faye — charismatic and always wearing her trademark heavy mascara — sang. Most episodes were taped at their sprawling complex just south of Charlotte, North Carolina.
The couple was so famous that they were often parodied by TV comedians for their lavish lifestyle and Tammy Faye's abundant makeup.
Sex scandal and financial crimes damage his empire
In March 1987, their empire began to crack when Bakker admitted to a sexual encounter with church clerk Jessica Hahn. Bakker was forced to resign from his own empire, turning over operations to pastor and broadcaster Jerry Falwell.
Tammy Faye stuck by Bakker, often with tears running down her mascara, even as many saw his downfall as a fitting symbol of the greed and hypocrisy of the 1980s.
Things only got worse.
In 1988, Bakker was indicted for mail fraud, wire fraud and conspiracy after an investigation of PTL's finances. He was convicted and sentenced to 45 years in federal prison, though the sentence was later reduced to eight years.
At a news conference after Bakker was found guilty, Tammy Faye stood in front of the microphones and sang the hymn, "On Christ the Solid Rock I Stand."
Their marriage crumbled and Tammy Faye divorced Bakker in 1992, just short of their 31st anniversary, while he was still in prison. She later married Roe Messner, a building contractor whose projects included the Heritage USA theme park. Messner was convicted of bankruptcy fraud in 1995 and spent about two years in prison.
Tammy Faye died of colon cancer in 2007.
Bakker was released on parole in 1994. He married his second wife, Lori, in 1998. The couple launched "The Jim Bakker Show" on the PTL Satellite Network five years later.
In June 2021, Bakker and his Morningside Church Productions Inc. settled a lawsuit accusing him of falsely claiming the health supplement Silver Solution could cure COVID-19. The settlement called for $156,000 in refunds to people who paid money or gave contributions to obtain the product in the early days of the pandemic.
The lawsuit said Bakker and a guest made the cure claim during 11 episodes in February and March of 2020.
Bakker and Tammy Faye had two children. He and his second wife adopted five children in 2002.

As Nandigram and Rejinagar constituencies in West Bengal go to the polls on October 6, several local journalists in Murshidabad district, where Rejinagar is located, have alleged that access to their news Facebook pages has been restricted in India. These outlets primarily covered Opposition parties and the limited campaigning they were able to carry out in the constituency.
The notices they received stated: “We repeatedly had to restrict access to content posted by you pursuant to legal requirements under India’s Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules… We have accordingly temporarily restricted access to your account for 7 days in India.”
Two Seats: Little in Terms of Electoral Contest
Byelections are being held in these constituencies because the elected representatives also won from other seats in the state elections earlier this year. The Nandigram assembly constituency has about 2.5 lakh people, with Muslims accounting for around 27% of the electorate. It is Suvendu Adhikari’s home constituency. In 2021, Adhikari defeated former chief minister Mamata Banerjee here by 1,956 votes. In the 2026 assembly polls, he won from Nandigram as well as Bhabanipur. He chose to retain the Bhabanipur seat where he defeated Banerjee, necessitating the byelection in Nandigram.
The Nandigram contest took an unexpected turn when the candidate of the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress faction, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination on September 18. Banerjee then decided to support Congress candidate Milan Pradhan. However, within hours of Banerjee announcing her support for Pradhan, he was arrested in connection with old cases related to the 2007 Nandigram violence. Congress and the TMC questioned the timing of the arrest, while the BJP said the police action was based on pending cases and involved no political intervention. He was later granted interim bail by the Calcutta high court.
Rejinagar presents a different electoral landscape, with Muslims accounting for around 69% of its electorate. The constituency was a closely watched seat in the 2026 assembly election. Aam Janata Unnyan Party (AJUP) leader Humayun Kabir won both Nowda and Rejinagar and subsequently vacated the latter, where his victory margin was more than 58,000 votes.
The Rejinagar by-election has seen little campaigning by the main Opposition candidates, who allege police intimidation and interference by the ruling party. The Banerjee-backed Trinamool Congress faction has fielded former three-term MLA Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, who had considered withdrawing from the contest before Banerjee persuaded him to stay. The Congress has fielded Abdullahil Kafi, while the Democratic TMC faction has nominated Safiuzzaman S K and the CPI(M) Saeed Asad Ali.
Kabir has alleged that police arrested 15 of his workers in what he calls false cases, while others have fled the area. He was also questioned twice over a viral audio clip. He says he has therefore halted major campaigning and is reaching voters primarily through Facebook, while his son continues to visit some areas. Independent candidate Saiful Islam, who is close to the AJUP leadership, was arrested on September 19.
With arrests, alleged intimidation, and lack of opposition campaigning, the elections in both the seats appear to offer little in the way of a competitive contest.
Facebook Pages Reporting Local News Restricted
With the Opposition campaign already muted in both constituencies, the election is also unfolding amid allegations of censorship in Rejinagar. Local journalists who reported on issues critical of the government or law enforcement, or covered Opposition campaigns, suddenly found their Facebook pages, which were their primary outlets for publishing their work, restricted in India.
Alt News identified at least 12 such pages: Murshidabad Global Times run by Asif Roni; Hariharpara Times Bangla run by Jabbar Sheikh; Murshidabad Today run by Swapan Karigar; Murshidabad Shironam run by Rinku; Murshidabad News Time run by Baktar Sk; Reporter Press run by Rajib Sheikh; M News TV run by Muhaimenul Haque; Bartabahi News run by Aminul Islam; Hi News run by Saidur Rahman; BNS News Bangla; AN Bangla News run by Abdus Samad; and News Front Digital run by Abdul Halim.
Swapan Karigar’s Murshidabad Today, which had a following of around 7.4 lakh, was among those worst affected. A practising journalist with more than 26 years of experience, he now has a restricted account, limiting his ability to report on politics ahead of the election.
Karigar said the page had been reporting allegations of intimidation by police made by residents who support Opposition parties, including AJUP and the Congress. “A lot of common people, who have aligned themselves with opposition parties like AJUP and Congress, people who have, say, walked in political rallies, have alleged that their family members, especially women and children, are being intimidated and tortured by police officials. They (the police) have visited these houses with 12-14 cars, even. A child was also pulled by her hair, and a woman was physically assaulted. They have totally created an atmosphere of fear and intimidation before the election. We were covering these incidents, upholding the truth. That is probably why our accounts have been withheld,” he told Alt News.
We spoke to Asif Roni, whose Facebook page, Murshidabad Global Times, had around 4.47 lakh followers before it was taken down on the night of October 1 — the same day chief minister Suvendu Adhikari visited Rejinagar. Roni said the page had recorded 39 million views in the preceding 28 days. Law enforcement officials told him that the page would be withheld for seven days.
“This happened once around April, right before the assembly election,” he said. “I used to run a different page called AN Bangla. It still hasn’t been reactivated. They shut quite a few pages then, and those haven’t been restored either. So I had to switch to Murshidabad GT, which used to be a backup page.”
Roni said that after the earlier restriction, a senior police official had told him that the page would be restored “after the election”.
Jabbar Sheikh, who runs Hariharpara Times Bangla, told us that his Facebook page, which had around 4.39 lakh followers, was taken down on September 30, after it published a report on Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury. “More than thirty pages have been restricted. The main reason is that we covered news about the Opposition parties, especially Humayun’s campaign. So there was possibly a political motive. It’s the Indian government that did it. The pages don’t show in India, although they would show in other countries,” Jabbar said.
This was the first time Jabbar had faced such a restriction. He, too, approached police, but said officials told him they had not ordered the restrictions. “They told us that Meta itself had found guideline violations and restricted the pages on that basis, and that cyber crime had no hand in it,” he said.
For a lot of local journalists, publishing news content on Facebook was their only source of livelihood.
It took Swapan Karigar six years to build Murshidabad Today. “This has never happened before. This was my only source of income. I know nothing apart from journalism. I have another small page with around 14,000 followers, and I am posting non-political content from there now. I can’t give up my profession, but I’m cutting down on political content for the time being,” he said. The page had around 24 million views before it was restricted.
Roni said around 25 to 30 such pages had been restricted across the district. When we asked why these pages had been targeted, he said he was told that they had published news that could be perceived as anti-government. “Mostly they’ve closed those who give a bit more coverage to the Opposition political parties’ news. For me, they restricted it after I posted my report on Adhir Chowdhury,” he said.
Roni now publishes from another page, MGT, which has around 15,000 followers. Jabbar is similarly posting content from a second page with barely 2,000 followers.
“All of our pages were monetised. Good money came from it, and a lot of us were getting by. Educated, unemployed youth started this trend alongside other things,” Roni said.
They are not Journalists, Says Murshidabad SP
We spoke to Sachin Makkar, superintendent of police, Murshidabad, who first asked us to “read the notice carefully”.
“Does the notice mention the police or the cyber crime wing? You should contact Meta about this. Does it say that the police restricted the pages?” he asked. When we pressed further, he said, “I do not have a lot to say on the matter. And they are not journalists; they are not accredited journalists. Whatever action has been taken, we have not done it. You can talk to Meta about the rest…”
It is worth noting that the notices received by the administrators say the pages were withheld pursuant to legal requirements. This indicates that the restrictions followed a legal request or complaint concerning the content on these pages, rather than being solely the result of Meta’s own content-moderation process.
We have written to Meta seeking details of the requests it received and the reasons for restricting the pages. This article will be updated if and when we receive a response.

Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix for ₹1,012.03 Cr in an all-cash deal, taking its total holding in the startup to 84.09%. The latest transaction is part of an agreement to acquire a total 38.18% stake from Plix’s founders and certain other shareholders. Marico plans to acquire 14.09% stake in July 2027. The consideration for this tranche will include a base amount of up to ₹592 Cr, along with additional payments linked to milestones. Marico said the investment in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals and its wholly owned subsidiary Juzio has helped broaden its addressable market across value-added foods and nutrition, while strengthening its presence in the growing personal care and wellness segments. Founded in 2020 by Satiya and Zaveri, Plix Life is a Mumbai-based D2C startup that sells a wide range of plant-based nutrition products, such as workout supplements, ingestible sunscreens, hair growth serums and skincare products. To note, Plix parent’s consolidated revenue nearly doubled to ₹864.31 Cr in FY26 from ₹432.84 Cr in FY25. Marico acquired 37.75% stake in D2C nutrition brand Plix for ₹369.01 Cr in July 2023, and it further acquired 25.25% of the paid-up share capital by May 2025. Plix’s cap table featured names like Guild Capital and RPSG Ventures. The deal is in line with Marico's broader push into high-growth consumer categories as the company looks to build businesses beyond its established portfolio of food, personal care and consumer products. Marico kicked off 2026 with an acquisition spree. Marico snapped up a 93.27% stake in gourmet popcorn brand 4700BC’s parent Zea Maize from PVR INOX for ₹226.8 Cr. In February, it picked up a 60% stake in Bengaluru-based plant-based protein startup Cosmix Wellness for ₹226 Cr. It also acquired a 75% stake in Vietnam-based Skinetiq Joint Stock Company for an estimated ₹262-350 Cr. The rapid growth of Plix comes as large FMCG companies continue to expand into newer consumer categories, particularly health, nutrition, personal care and wellness. For instance, FMCG major ITC completed the acquisition of 100% of Yoga Bar’s parent Sproutlife Foods, buying the remaining 52.5% stake for around ₹645 Cr, only a few weeks ago. Prior to that, FMCG major Emami acquired a 60% stake in IncNut Digital, the parent entity of D2C beauty and personal care brands Vedix and SkinKraft, for up to ₹321 Cr in an all-cash transaction, in May. Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) also acquired the remaining 49% stake in OZiva parent Zywie Ventures for ₹824 Cr, in February this year.

73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it
- Published
As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.
Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.
When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.
"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.
I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.
Watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.
From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.
Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.
The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.
As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology company Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.
And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.
"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane says.
"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles."
Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.
Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.
Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.
Kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.
After getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.
Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.
1 of 4
Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.
"I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," says Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?
"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play."
There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.
Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.
"I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he says. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.
"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.
"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with."
Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 - in a front two.
"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he says. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball."
Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.
"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.
"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre."
Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.
"I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off."
It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.
"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he says. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track]."
1 of 3
The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.
Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder - something he recognises and exploits.
Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.
"These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.
"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.
"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.
"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.
"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back."
1 of 3
With the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.
Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.
He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.
In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

If one form of energy becomes the cheapest, most secure, and cleanest, you’d probably adjust your economy to use more of it, right?
That’s one of the ideas underpinning a report the International Energy Agency issued last week about the global move toward electrification. Fatih Birol, head of the IEA, discussed some of the concepts from the report the following day at the United Nations.
“Many, many years in the energy world, we had three choices in front of us. Shall I choose the most secure energy option? Shall I choose the most economic energy option? Or shall I choose the cleanest energy option?” he asked. “We have to make choices, we have to make trade-offs but when we look at the world today, for the first time in years, all of these three objectives are getting aligned.”
Birol’s referring to the “energy trilemma,” a concept in energy and economics research about the need to balance cost, security and environmental impact of sources and systems. He said those priorities are increasingly aligning in part because of the Iran war, which has driven up fuel prices and exacerbated concerns about energy security.
It’s notable that the leader of the world’s leading energy research organization is so optimistic about electrification. I reached out to energy researchers this week to get their reaction.
But first, some numbers:
With $100 worth of gasoline, an internal-combustion-engine car would go 862 miles; with $100 worth of electricity, an electric vehicle would go 2,310 miles—nearly a threefold advantage for the EV.
For home heating, $100 would buy enough fuel for a gas boiler to provide 30 days of heating; it would also fund enough electricity for a heat pump to provide 42 days of heating—a 40 percent edge for the heat pump.
The figures are 2025 global averages from the IEA report, and the gaps are probably larger today with gasoline and natural gas experiencing price spikes that exceed rising electricity costs.

In a three-day strategic dialogue, Belgium and WHO reviewed progress in their longstanding partnership, and agreed to further boost their collaboration on universal health coverage, health-systems strengthening and equitable access to essential vaccines, medicines and health technologies.
The Belgian delegation – headed by H.E. Christophe Payot, Ambassador of Belgium to the United Nations and other international organizations in Geneva – discussed issues of strategic importance, exchanged views on how to smoothly align WHO strategic directions and Belgium's development cooperation priorities in the context of an evolving global health landscape.
The partners exchanged updates on Belgium's support to global health areas brought in the spotlight during the Belgian presidency of Council of the European Union in 2024. WHO was represented by leadership and technical experts from Headquarters and from the Regional Offices for Africa and for Europe.
"After listening to the leaders and experts of WHO we now better understand how they are navigating these challenging times", said Mr Koen Van Acoleyen, Minister Counselor at the Permanent Representation of Belgium to the UN. "We are honoured that we can walk this road together."
Accelerating equitable access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies
The partners reviewed the current status and the most noticeable results achieved by the Access to Medicines programme funded by Belgium. WHO illustrated its work and challenges with an example of country-level implementation in Senegal. It also explained WHO's policies and work on equitable access and local production. Both parties recognized a shared goal for sustainability of the Access to Medicines initiative, as market shaping is key to ensure long-term success.
Health emergencies and pandemic prevention, preparedness and response
Discussions covered WHO's role in strengthening the global architecture for health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience, including the pandemic agreement negotiations and the One Health approach. WHO's crucial field work on health emergency response was demonstrated by presenting the activities in Gaza. The debate also touched upon threats posed by acceleration of biological risks and zoonoses, along with WHO engagement, in particular, risk mitigation.
Universal Health Coverage (UHC)
Elaborating on progress made on UHC-Partnership, the participants reviewed results achieved by WHO with Belgium support in the period 2021-2024, specifically in Belgium's partner countries. They discussed the way forward, exploring the potential for enhanced collaboration at country level, including eventual alignment between WHO country office programmes and Belgium's country level bilateral cooperation. Examples included a summary of the work and challenges at country level from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The visitors listened to a recap of WHO's policies and work on mental health in the context of primary health care.
The partners also reviewed progress in other areas of collaboration on WHO programmes supported by Belgium, such as Neglected Tropical Diseases and Sexual, Reproductive Health and Rights. The review underpinned the importance of an evidence-based approach in these areas.
WHO appreciates Belgium's commitment and engagement, displayed by the participation of representatives of the country's Federal government as well as the Flemish and Walloon governments. "We thank you for your support, honesty, and strong engagement for global health", said Dr Catharina Boehme, Assistant Director-General, External Relations and Governing Bodies. "Your efforts in supporting our work in Mozambique and Senegal are clear examples of the crucial work we accomplish together".
Looking into the future
The partners discussed ways forward for the Belgium-WHO collaboration framework and multi-year agreement, including progress towards a renewed WHO-Belgium Country Cooperation Strategy.
The enhanced collaboration between Belgium and WHO will support a strong global health agenda under the WHO 14th General Programme of Work (GPW14). There was a shared vision that UHC and health systems strengthening being at the heart of GPW14 ambitions will be taken as essential scope in WHO's ongoing prioritization work.
"We recognize WHO as a trustworthy partner in global health. We felt proud hearing how crucial our support is to the Organization and how it is having a positive impact at country, regional, and global levels", said Mr Dirk Brems, Director of Thematic and Multilateral Cooperation, Directorate-General Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid. "It's important we continue these discussions as we tread uncharted territories, and we look forward to working together for strong and sustained multilateralism".

Japan raises residency fee for foreign nationals by twenty-fold
- Published
Japan has raised fees for foreigners looking to reside in the country, with the cost of permanent residency going up 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955).
Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements.
Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours.
The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim ito manage its rapidly growing foreign population.
In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years. Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations".
Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage.
Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year. This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change.
Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year.
In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows.
"To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote.
Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay.
From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.
Applicants who face financial hardship or are designated as refugees would be granted discounts.
Aspiring permanent residents must now also earn a stable income at or above the Japanese average. Latest data released in July puts average household income at 5.75 million yen as of 2024.
From April next year, permanent residency applicants will face even tighter requirements, including basic Japanese language proficiency. This has led to a surge in enrollments at Japanese language schools as well as people signing up to take the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test, local media reported.
Applicants' expected pension benefits must also be equivalent to that of someone who has enrolled into the employee pension system for 30 years, although the value of one's financial assets can be considered if their expected pension benefits fall short.

The Jan Swasthya Abhiyan (JSA) and the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment have called for regulation of charges levied by private hospitals and ceilings on trade margins for medicines, medical devices and medical consumables, amid renewed scrutiny by the Supreme Court of pricing practices in hospital pharmacies.
The groups, in a statement issued on Monday (October 5, 2026), said patients continued to face high and arbitrary charges for treatment, medicines and consumables, with limited avenues to challenge hospital bills.
The Supreme Court has recently questioned steep markups on medicines sold through hospital pharmacies and practices that require patients to purchase medicines from hospital-linked pharmacies. The court has also asked the government to examine regulation of trade margins.
Pricing vs determining charge
“The problem extended beyond the pricing of individual medicines to the broader question of how private hospitals determine charges for procedures, services and consumables. Private healthcare has expanded enormously in India, but regulation has simply not kept pace,” said Abhay Shukla, co-convener, JSA. He added that patients often had little bargaining power at healthcare facilities.
The Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 provides a framework for registration and regulation of clinical establishments and envisages standardisation of services and charges. However, its implementation is not uniform across the country, and several States have their own legislation or regulatory arrangements.
The groups said the absence of a uniform mechanism to regulate hospital charges had left patients vulnerable to hefty bills, particularly for prolonged hospitalisation and procedures involving multiple medicines, devices and consumables.
They are now demanding that the Centre and States introduce ceilings on charges levied by private hospitals for procedures, services and treatment and establish accessible, time-bound mechanisms through which patients can challenge excessive or unjustified bills.
The groups have also called for regulation of trade margins on medicines, medical devices and other medical consumables.
K.M. Gopakumar, co-convener, Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment, said that the maximum retail price (MRP) cannot become a licence to charge patients many times the procurement price.
The group has also cited earlier concerns raised by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) regarding margins in pharmaceutical sales and incentives created when hospitals or hospital pharmacies control the products patients are required to purchase.
Financial incentives for doctors
Raising concern over the effect of financial incentives on clinical decision-making, Gayatri Sharma, a community health physician and researcher, said revenue-linked incentives could put pressure on doctors to increase investigations or procedures.
“Doctors should be able to make treatment decisions solely on the basis of what is medically necessary for the patient,” she said, calling for the National Medical Commission (NMC) to examine incentive-linked remuneration practices for doctors.
The group, in its statement, has called for a stronger public healthcare system alongside regulation of private providers, including increased public health spending and strengthening of government hospitals to provide accessible care. The demands include immediate regulation of trade margins on medicines, medical devices and consumables; ceilings on private hospital charges; a competition-law review of potentially anti-competitive practices; and an independent and time-bound grievance redress mechanism for patients.

NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday accused the Election Commission of overseeing "mass manipulation and rigging" during the West Bengal assembly polls. He further demanded accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as well as other two election commissioners along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah."More skeletons are tumbling out of the Election Omission of India’s closet. Clearly the PM-HM strategy was to somehow capture and win the West Bengal Assembly elections at any cost. It was a text book case of mass manipulation and rigging which was overseen by the CEC. The puppet has of course to go but the two puppeteers too have to be held accountable. They stand brutally exposed and now it is only a matter of time for them to meet their reckoning," Ramesh wrote in a post on X."Today, MPs of the INDIA janbandhan plus other Opposition MPs who have also been invited will be marching peacefully to the Election Commission of India to demand the CEC's resignation. Looks like the Parliament complex is already under an unprecedented security siege showing the extreme nervousness of the puppeteer pair," he added.
Jairam Ramesh's latest attack on EC
Ramesh's remarks followed a media report claiming that judges of more than a dozen tribunals appointed in West Bengal on the Supreme Court's directions to hear appeals related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), including those involving 27 lakh deleted electors, had flagged gaps in a digital portal created by the Election Commission's IT division.The Congress has stepped up its criticism of the poll panel amid a wider dispute over the SIR exercise. The opposition's latest attack also comes after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modification to Form 6, the application used by eligible voters to seek inclusion in electoral rolls.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said, "We will examine all the decisions. If any decision is not in accordance with the law, we will annul it. You know the power of the court."The bench also said, "any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When records are produced, we would like to see who has modified it".The Congress and other opposition parties have demanded Kumar's resignation, alleging that changes to Form 6 were made unilaterally during the SIR process. Rahul Gandhi on Monday said the CEC and others involved in what he called a "criminal assault on democracy" would be held accountable.
Separately, a report by The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders, many concerning the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has rejected concerns arising from the reported differences, saying divergent views are part of institutional deliberations and that its orders have full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

When the international friendly between India and Brazil was announced, many dismissed it as a farce until the official confirmation landed. The prospect of a side ranked outside the top-135 locking horns with the five-time world champion, currently perched at World No. 6, sounded like a grotesque mismatch — a lamb to the slaughter, in the eyes of the sceptics.
But after two matches against World Cup-playing nations, Panama and Brazil, the Blue Tigers will not consider the exercise entirely futile. They came within a whisker of beating Panama, a team ranked 94 places above them, before conceding a late equaliser, and then put up a valiant show at the Salt Lake Stadium, eventually succumbing 0-4 to Brazil.
At full-time against Panama, the fans gave a thunderous round of applause to the team’s exertions, unanimously agreeing that it was their finest performance in recent memory. And at the end of the second match, the conversation withing Indian football circles had shifted from ‘How many goals would India lose by?’ to ‘India could have conceded two fewer goals against Brazil.’
This is the shift India needs: the conviction that the Blue Tigers can actually roar despite having no regular league football for months.
ALSO READ | India loses to Ancelotti’s new-look Brazil in Kolkata friendly
“We have to play more (such) matches for experience. But from my side, I think the players did not leave any stone unturned in terms of their efforts. I got them to play defensively; they contributed to the build-up and attack,” India’s coach Khalid Jamil said.
Winds of change under Jamil
Several factors contributed to the team turning the tide. Jamil, for the first time, got his full set of players at his disposal in the national camp.
In India’s previous matches at the Unity Cup and the CAFA Nations Cup, several players from Mohun Bagan Super Giant were not released by the club for the fixtures because they were outside the official FIFA window.
Logistics did not help India’s cause either — its key striker Ryan Williams could not get his No Objection Certificate to play against Bangladesh, while senior defender Sandesh Jhingan suffered an injury during the CAFA Nations Cup that ruled him out of the rest of the tournament.
This time around, Jamil also made some bold calls: a younger squad with 11 changes from the team that played in the Unity Cup, dropping several first-team regulars like Jhingan, Lallianzuala Chhangte, Brandon Fernandes and Jeakson Singh.
“I have selected players according to their merits and performance. It’s not like we have selected 26 players. We don’t have to take all of them. If someone isn’t performing well, he will go back within two days. It’s not like I didn’t give anyone a chance. I saw everyone. Whoever deserves to be there, I gave him a 100% chance,” Jamil told PTI in an interview.
The message was unambiguous: he needed a hungry lot, one that could attack and defend with equal intensity.
And the effect was immediate. After what felt like ages, India exuded confidence right from the get-go against Panama.
Missed opportunities were not followed by slouched shoulders, but rather used as motivation to do better, and the renewed optimism was rewarded at the end of the first half as Williams put the Blue Tigers in front after latching onto a lovely floated ball from Akash Mishra.
A heavily reshuffled Panama looked out of sorts for most of the game, only to rely on long-range attempts, like that from Omar Valencia — a beauty nonetheless — that earned them a draw. A few years ago, such a strike would have diminished spirits in the Indian camp, but Jamil’s men kept at it and almost retook the lead if not for some profligate finishing in front of goal.
At training sessions too, Jamil has looked different — very active, unusually vocal and ruthless with select training for certain players.
His reputation for ‘parking the bus’ also seemed a thing of the distant past. India no longer sat back; it marched forward and kept attacking until Williams found the net. India tried two more shots, which were blocked. Williams also came close to scoring against Brazil, with Mauro Junior making a goal-line clearance.
Despite an impressive showing against Brazil, Jamil sought more from the substitutes and did not hold back after the game, issuing a veiled threat to players who would slack. “If a player comes on, they have to be prepared. Today, there were 11 changes, so we have tried everybody. They have to capitalise on the chance; otherwise, they will not get another chance,” Jamil said.
Getting back to basics
Jamil has tried several shapes, including a three-man backline, a false nine, and a conventional 4-3-3, but might have found the solution in 4-4-2 — a formation in which India lined up under Stephen Constantine, with Bhaichung Bhutia and Jeje Lalpekhlua leading the attack.
This is the formation that saw India break into the top 100 of the FIFA rankings under the English coach, and in which it shone through, qualifying for the AFC Asian Cup after 27 years. With quick wingers and Williams offering an outlet up front, India has looked more threatening in transition under Jamil.
The biggest highlight, however, for the team is having Williams in an Indian jersey. The forward looked a class apart on the pitch, making runs behind the defenders, clearing corner kicks and then testing the goalkeeper from the box — Williams did everything that was expected of him and more.
ALSO READ | One of the best results of my tenure with India: Khalid Jamil after Panama draw
And his performance could spark a discussion on allowing more Indian-origin players in the national team. India’s performances against Panama and Brazil did not lack effort; it missed team chemistry in finishing. Jamil will look to chisel that, with the team travelling to New Zealand, another World Cup-playing nation, in the next international window.
Playing against high-ranked opponents also looks like a positive step, for the rankings do affect the morale of any team. As long as the All India Football Federation is not hurt financially, these matches provide an invaluable opportunity to earn high ranking points. For example, a draw against Tajikistan (ranked 101st) earned India 1.33 points, while the same outcome against Panama (ranked 44th) gave it 3.19 points.
India has a long way to go before it realistically thinks of rubbing shoulders with teams like Panama, Brazil and Uruguay in the World Cup. But playing against them with consistent aggression and fluid attacking football is a refreshing change — one that gives an indication of better things to come if allowed to continue.

It is probably impossible to overstate how complex a brain is: A network of billions of intertwined neurons forming an intricate anatomy, capable of working on the millisecond scale to perceive reality, detect sensations, create plans, and take actions.
“All of this is incredibly complicated, and so of course the challenge that we face as neuroscientists and as physicians treating brain disorders is how can we hope to make headway without tools that match the complexity and the precision of the brain?” said Karl Deisseroth, a Stanford University and Howard Hughes Medical Institute researcher who on Monday won the 2026 Nobel Prize for Medicine, alongside German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel, for work developing such tools.
“Our perception of reality and all our inner subjective states come from cells, and so the appropriate tool that would be matched to how the brain works would be something that was fast and could be targeted to individual cells or individual types of cells,” he said in an interview after the announcement.

When Anastasia Sevriukova first noticed blood in her stool at age 25, she didn't tell anyone at first — not her then-boyfriend or her mom.
Her Google search narrowed the cause down to either colon cancer — which seemed extremely unlikely due to her lack of family history — or hemorrhoids.
"I Googled 'I had oysters. Did the shell cut my intestine?'" Sevriukova, now 27, told Business Insider. She tried hemorrhoid creams that didn't work.
When the bleeding persisted for months, she saw a primary care physician in September 2024, who put her on a four-month waitlist to see a GI.
In the meantime, Sevriukova kept living her life in St. Louis, Missouri. She worked as an engineer for Boeing's military branch. In her free time, she learned to watercolor and had one of her paintings displayed at a local exhibition.
Even at the end of 2024, when she was told that she'd be laid off from Boeing in mid-January 2025, things were looking up. Shortly after, Sevriukova, who is Ukrainian, was offered a position at a San Francisco startup developing drones to be used by Ukraine in the ongoing war — a dream job. Weeks later, she got engaged.
"The whole month was a rollercoaster," she said. Between plans to start the new job, move to a new city, and eventually build a family with her now-fiancé, Sevriukova was excited about the future.
Then, four days after the engagement, she was diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer.
"Everything had to pretty much stop because I was very, very sick," she said. "It was really difficult to accept that I need to take a break for now."
She thought she was tired because of work
In the months leading up to her scheduled GI appointment in January 2025, Sevriukova frequently felt very fatigued. "I was like 'I'm just tired from work, I have to do a lot,'" she said.
Then there was the date night a week before the doctor's visit. She and her fiancé went to a wine-and-pizza bar. Suddenly, Sevriukova felt drunk from one glass.
After her diagnosis, she learned that she had anemia, a common symptom of colon cancer. She had a hemoglobin level of 8 g/dL (a normal range for women is 12 to 15.5 g/dL).
A CT scan revealed her stage 4 colon cancer diagnosis, and explained her feeling drunk off one drink: It was a sign of her liver not functioning properly, because the cancer had spread to it.
Given her diagnosis, Sevriukova declined her job offer. The couple moved to Rochester, Minnesota, where Sevriukova's mother lives. Upon seeing her new oncologist, she was put on an iron infusion before starting cancer treatment. She also underwent genetic testing and learned she had no predisposition for cancer, such as Lynch syndrome.
"It was a stroke of bad luck," she said.
A breakneck decision about her future fertility
Sevriukova's oncologist told her that she would most likely lose her ability to have kids after side effects from chemotherapy.
Because he wanted to start her treatment right away, he gave her two weeks to retrieve and freeze her eggs. Sevriukova was referred to the Mayo Clinic and decided to go through with the procedure.
"It was very physically and emotionally demanding," Sevriukova said. "I was also trying to process at the same time, the fact that whatever eggs they can get, that's all they got." She had her egg extraction in March 2025. Two days later, she started chemotherapy and antibody therapy, which her doctors selected after a liver biopsy identified features of her tumor relevant to treatment.
By that point, she was exhausted from two weeks of hormone therapy to produce as many eggs as possible, plus the frequent bloodwork and ultrasound appointments during the monitoring phase. The egg retrieval itself was also painful and led to spotting by the time she began cancer treatment.
"Yet, I do not regret it at all," Sevriukova said. "It was the best decision I've made."
She took a break from both treatments in June 2025, when she was prepped for surgery on her colon and the installation of a hepatic artery infusion (HAI) pump, which channels chemotherapy medication directly into the liver.
There were complications with the surgery. She had a rare bowel leak because the incision in her colon was not sealed properly, leading to an infection in her abdomen. "That is probably the most pain I have experienced in my life," she said, spending 20 days in the hospital. The resulting surgery left Sevriukova with scars and a stoma bag, a waste collection pouch outside of her abdomen.
"I could not stop crying for days, and the nurses didn't even know what to do, how to console me," she said. "My body doesn't look like what it used to look like a year ago, and body image is a huge, huge aspect of a young woman's life."
She needed a liver transplant
From the beginning, Sevriukova had "too many tumors to count" on her liver. Even when her scans were clear, the tumors would quickly resurface the moment she stopped chemo. "I never know when the cancer decides to mutate and take over," she said.
Sevriukova was eventually able to get a liver transplant in June 2026, which left her cancer-free for three months. Then, in August 2026, a CT scan revealed a few small tumors on her lungs. She will soon resume chemotherapy and antibody therapy.
Sevriukova has gradually adjusted to her new normal. She said that when she's in treatment, her mom, sister, and fiancé take turns staying with her at the hospital and talking to doctors on her behalf.
The side effects of treatment have been so debilitating that Sevriukova can't work — something she found devastating at the start of treatment. Instead, she's taking a full semester of computer science courses from a local community college, with the aim of getting her master's and advancing her career.
Still, she can never get fully used to the nausea and appetite loss right after each chemo treatment. "You just have to always roll with the punches," she said. "Right now I'm a little more used to those punches than I was at the beginning, but it's still really, really difficult."
She said the experience changed her emotionally. It's also made her realize how taboo colon cancer is, from talking about symptoms like rectal bleeding to living with a stoma bag.
"Even right now, it's a little uncomfortable to say," she said. "It's so vulnerable and makes it so difficult to talk about it, to bring it up to friends, to family, but it has to be done."

New Delhi: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was briefly detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday after security personnel stopped an INDIA bloc march towards the Election Commission headquarters in the national capital. She was taken inside a police van along with several other protesters before being released.
Videos of the incident have surfaced on social media, showing a high-voltage protest unfolding on the streets of Delhi as opposition MPs were stopped while marching towards the poll panel's office.
Priyanka Gandhi Detained During Protest
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was among the INDIA bloc leaders and workers who were stopped by security personnel during the march. She was subsequently taken into a police van along with other protesters.
Visuals from the spot show Priyanka being escorted towards the vehicle amid slogans and a gathering of opposition supporters. She was later released.
The detention happened after INDIA bloc MPs marched from the Parliament House complex towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Rahul Gandhi, Kharge Lead March
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge were among the opposition leaders participating in the protest.
The march was stopped by police on the stretch between NITI Aayog and Akashvani Bhavan, with protesters prevented from proceeding towards the Election Commission headquarters.
After being stopped, opposition MPs sat on the road and staged a dharna. Protesters raised slogans including “BJP hai CEC hai” and “Vote chor, gaddi chhod”, while some carried cutouts depicting Gyanesh Kumar in an RSS uniform.
Why Is INDIA Bloc Protesting?
The opposition's protest is centred on demands for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and allegations concerning the electoral roll revision process.
INDIA bloc parties have raised concerns over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, alleging that the process could result in the deletion of legitimate voters. Opposition leaders have described their broader campaign as a fight against alleged “vote theft”.
